sentences.zh: 顧榮

translations.literal: Gu Rong
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong

sentences.zh: 顧榮，字彥先，吳國吳人也，為南土著姓。

translations.literal: Gu Rong, courtesy name Yanxian, was a native of Wu in the Wu region; his clan counted among the great southern lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, whose courtesy name was Yanxian, hailed from Wu in the old Wu heartland, and his family belonged to one of the eminent southern houses.

sentences.zh: 祖雍，吳丞相。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong was chancellor of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gu Yong had served as chief minister under Wu.

sentences.zh: 父穆，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Mu was governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu Mu held the post of prefect of Yidu commandery.

sentences.zh: 榮機神朗悟，弱冠仕吳，為黃門侍郎、太子輔義都尉。

translations.literal: Rong's faculties were keen and clear; at the capping age he entered Wu's service as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and as Adjutant for Supporting Righteousness to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong was intellectually acute; still in his early twenties he took office under Wu as a palace attendant at the Yellow Gates and as adjutant mentoring the heir apparent in moral duty.

sentences.zh: 吳平，與陸機兄弟同入洛，時人號為「三俊。

translations.literal: When Wu had been pacified, he entered Luoyang together with Lu Ji and his brothers, and people of the time styled them the "three outstanding talents.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu he traveled to Luoyang alongside Lu Ji and his brothers, and contemporaries hailed them as the "three outstanding talents"—the quotation opening here trails the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 」例拜為郎中，歷尚書郎、太子中舍人、廷尉正。

translations.literal: " By precedent he was appointed gentleman langye, then served successively as gentleman of the Masters of Writing, attendant in the household of the heir apparent, and rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He received routine appointment as gentleman langye and rose through senior secretary posts, service in the heir apparent's household, and the rectifier's bench at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 恆縱酒酣暢，謂友人張翰曰：「惟酒可以忘憂，但無如作病何耳。」

translations.literal: He constantly indulged in wine until exhilarated, and said to his friend Zhang Han, "Only wine can make one forget cares; but nothing can be done about its making one sick."
translations.idiomatic: He often drank his way into heedless cheer and told his friend Zhang Han, "Wine alone can banish sorrow—if only it did not also lay you low with illness."

sentences.zh: 會趙王倫誅淮南王允，收允僚屬付廷尉，皆欲誅之，榮平心處當，多所全宥。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Zhao, Lun, executed the Prince of Huainan, Yun; Yun's subordinates were seized and delivered to the Minister of Justice, and all wished to execute them, but Rong weighed cases impartially and largely spared them.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao Sima Lun eliminated Prince Huainan Sima Yun, Yun's staff were handed to the judiciary for mass execution; Gu Rong adjudicated calmly and preserved many lives.

sentences.zh: 及倫篡位，倫子虔為大將軍，以榮為長史。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped the throne, Lun's son Qian became grand general and appointed Rong chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun seized power, his son Sima Qian became grand general and named Gu Rong chief clerk on his staff.

sentences.zh: 初，榮與同僚宴飲，見執炙者貌狀不凡，有欲炙之色，榮割炙啖之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while feasting with colleagues, Rong saw that the attendant turning the roast looked extraordinary and showed longing for the meat; Rong cut roast meat and fed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking with fellow officials, Gu Rong noticed the spit-turner carried himself with uncommon dignity and seemed to hunger for the roast; Gu Rong sliced meat for him to eat.

sentences.zh: 坐者問其故，榮曰：「豈有終日執之而不知其味！

translations.literal: Those seated asked his reason, and Rong said, "How can one handle it all day and not know its taste!
translations.idiomatic: Guests asked why; Gu Rong replied, "Can anyone turn the spit from dawn to dusk and never taste what he cooks?

sentences.zh: 」及倫敗，榮被執，將誅，而執炙者為督率，遂救之，得免。

translations.literal: " When Lun fell, Rong was seized and about to be executed, but the roast-handler had become a supervising officer and rescued him; he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun fell, Gu Rong was arrested and marked for execution—yet that same attendant now led guards and repaid the kindness, saving him from the blade.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏召為大司馬主簿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Jiong, summoned him to serve as chief clerk to the grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Sima Jiong called him up as chief clerk on the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 冏擅權驕恣，榮懼及禍，終日昏酣，不綜府事，以情告友人長樂馮熊。

translations.literal: Jiong monopolized power and behaved wantonly; Rong feared calamity would reach him, drank himself into a stupor every day, neglected bureau business, and confided in his friend Feng Xiong of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong grew arrogant and lawless; Gu Rong, dreading implication, spent his days drunk and idle in office until he unburdened himself to Feng Xiong of Changle.

sentences.zh: 熊謂冏長史葛旟曰：「以顧榮為主簿，所以甄拔才望，委以事機，不復計南北親疏，欲平海內之心也。

translations.literal: Feng said to Jiong's chief clerk Ge Yu, "Making Gu Rong chief clerk was meant to elevate men of talent and reputation and entrust them with critical duties, without weighing northern versus southern ties—a mind set on pacifying the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Feng told Ge Yu, Gu Rong's appointment was meant to honor southern talent and delegate real responsibility without petty regional bias—proof of a ruler intent on reuniting the land.

sentences.zh: 今府大事殷，非酒客之政。

translations.literal: Now the bureau's affairs are heavy and pressing; this is not work for a drunkard.
translations.idiomatic: The office now groans under urgent business; a wine-soaked placeholder cannot run it.

sentences.zh: 」旟曰：「榮江南望士，且居職日淺，不宜輕代易之。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Rong is a noted scholar of the south and has served only briefly; he should not lightly be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Yu answered, "Gu Rong is a southern gentleman of high standing and has barely warmed the seat; shifting him rashly would send the wrong signal.

sentences.zh: 」熊曰：「可轉為中書侍郎，榮不失清顯，而府更收實才。

translations.literal: " Feng said, "Transfer him to palace gentleman attendant; Rong keeps honor and visibility while the bureau gains a capable hand.
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied, "Make him a palace gentleman attendant instead—Gu Rong stays eminent while you gain a sober administrator.

sentences.zh: 」旟然之，白冏，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: " Yu agreed, reported to Jiong, and Rong was appointed palace gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Yu concurred, informed Sima Jiong, and Gu Rong moved to the palace gentleman attendant post.

sentences.zh: 在職不復飲酒。

translations.literal: In that office he no longer drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: He quit drinking entirely once reassigned.

sentences.zh: 人或問之曰：「何前醉而後醒邪？

translations.literal: Someone asked him, "Why drunk before and sober after?
translations.idiomatic: An acquaintance teased him: "How is it you were soused yesterday but clear-headed today?

sentences.zh: 」榮懼罪，乃復更飲。

translations.literal: " Rong feared giving offense and therefore drank again.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, anxious that candor might invite trouble, went back to the cup.

sentences.zh: 與州里楊彥明書曰：「吾為齊王主簿，恆慮禍及，見刀與繩，每欲自殺，但人不知耳。

translations.literal: In a letter to Yang Yanming of his commandery he wrote, "As chief clerk to the Prince of Qi I constantly feared disaster; seeing knife and rope I often wished to kill myself—only no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to his townsman Yang Yanming, "Serving Sima Jiong as chief clerk, I lived in terror; at the sight of blade or cord I nearly took my own life—secretly, where no one could see.

sentences.zh: 」及旟誅，榮以討葛旟功，封喜興伯，轉太子中庶子。

translations.literal: " When Yu was executed, Rong for merit in the campaign against Ge Yu was enfeoffed as Baron of Xixing and transferred to senior attendant in the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Yu died, Gu Rong earned the barony of Xixing for helping bring him down and was promoted to senior attendant in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂為驃騎，復以榮為長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Changsha, Yi, became commander-in-chief, again he appointed Rong chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changsha Sima Yi, upon becoming chief commander, once more named Gu Rong chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 乂敗，轉成都王穎丞相從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Yi was defeated, he was transferred to serve as gentleman consultant on the staff of the Prince of Chengdu, Ying's, chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi's defeat Gu Rong became an adviser on Prince Chengdu Sima Ying's chancellery staff.

sentences.zh: 惠帝幸臨漳，以榮兼侍中，遣行園陵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui visited Linzhang, Rong was additionally appointed attendant-in-ordinary and sent to inspect the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's progress to Linzhang brought Gu Rong a concurrent palace-attendant title and a mission to survey the imperial burial parks.

sentences.zh: 會張方據洛，不得進，避之陳留。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Fang held Luoyang; he could not advance and withdrew to Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang's occupation of Luoyang blocked the journey, forcing him to shelter in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 及帝西遷長安，徵為散騎常侍，以世亂不應，遂還吳。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved west to Chang'an, he was summoned as serving attendant-in-ordinary; because the age was in chaos he did not answer the call and returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The court's removal to Chang'an brought a summons to serving attendant-in-ordinary, but he declined amid the turmoil and went home to Wu.

sentences.zh: 東海王越聚兵於徐州，以榮為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, gathered troops at Xuzhou and appointed Rong army advisory libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Donghai Sima Yue, rallying forces in Xuzhou, appointed Gu Rong army advisory libationer.

sentences.zh: 屬廣陵相陳敏反，南渡江，逐揚州刺史劉機、丹陽內史王曠，阻兵據州，分置子弟為列郡，收禮豪桀，有孫氏鼎峙之計。

translations.literal: When Chen Min, the administrator of Guangling, rebelled, crossed south of the Yangzi, drove out Governor Liu Ji of Yang Province and Interior Administrator Wang Kuang of Danyang, held the province with arms, installed his sons in commandery posts, gathered bold spirits, and harbored plans like Sun Quan's tripartite division.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangling prefect Chen Min rose in revolt, marched south of the river, expelled Yang provincial governor Liu Ji and Danyang interior administrator Wang Kuang, seized the region by force, parcelled posts among his kin, courted local heroes, and dreamed of another Sun-family partition.

sentences.zh: 假榮右將軍、丹陽內史。

translations.literal: He provisionally appointed Rong general of the right and interior administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min named Gu Rong acting general of the right and interior administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 榮數踐危亡之際，恆以恭遜自勉。

translations.literal: Rong had repeatedly trodden the brink of ruin and constantly practiced deference to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong had survived one crisis after another and habitually softened his manner to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 會敏欲誅諸士人，榮說之曰：「中國喪亂，胡夷內侮，觀太傅今日不能復振華夏，百姓無復遺種。

translations.literal: When Chen Min intended to kill various scholars, Rong remonstrated: "The central lands lie in ruin and barbarians press inward; observing the grand tutor's situation, he cannot restore Huaxia—the common people will leave no seed.
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Min prepared to purge educated men, Gu Rong urged him, "The heartland is shattered and frontier peoples pour in; even the grand tutor cannot revive the Chinese heartland—the folk may be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 江南雖有石冰之寇，人物尚全。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, though there was Shi Bing's ravages, persons of talent remain intact.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river, despite Shi Bing's raid, society still stands largely whole.

sentences.zh: 榮常憂無竇氏、孫、劉之策，有以存之耳。

translations.literal: Rong has constantly worried that without a Dou or a Sun-Liu strategy there would be no way to preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: I have long feared that lacking a Dou-style patronage or Sun-Liu-style leadership we could not preserve this refuge.

sentences.zh: 今將軍懷神武之略，有孫吳之能，功勳效於已著，勇略冠於當世，帶甲數萬，舳艫山積，上方雖有數州，亦可傳檄而定也。

translations.literal: Now the general cherishes godlike martial strategy and abilities rivaling Sun Wu; merit already shines and daring surpasses the age; armored soldiers number in the tens of thousands and ships pile like mountains; though the upper reaches still hold several provinces, they could be settled with a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: You wield strategic genius compared to Sun Wu, your victories already awe the age, your tens of thousands of armored men and mountain stacks of hulls could swallow the remaining provinces by sheer manifesto.

sentences.zh: 若能委信君子，各得盡懷，散蒂芥之恨，塞讒諂之口，則大事可圖也。

translations.literal: If you can entrust gentlemen of integrity and let each pour out his mind, scatter petty grudges, and shut the mouths of slanderers, great deeds may be planned.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly empower trustworthy scholars, air every grievance, silence backbiters, you might yet achieve something lasting.

sentences.zh: 」敏納其言，悉引諸豪族委任之。

translations.literal: " Chen Min accepted his words and drew in all the powerful clans, delegating authority to them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min took the advice and pulled every great clan into his administration.

sentences.zh: 敏仍遣甘卓出橫江，堅甲利器，盡以委之。

translations.literal: Chen Min still sent Gan Zhuo out toward Hengjiang, handing him hardened armor and keen weapons in full trust.
translations.idiomatic: He still dispatched Gan Zhuo toward Hengjiang with the best armor and arms at his disposal.

sentences.zh: 榮私于卓曰：「若江東之事可濟，當共成之。

translations.literal: Privately Rong said to Zhuo, "If the east-of-the-river enterprise can succeed, we should finish it together.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong whispered to Gan Zhuo, "If this lower-Yangzi venture can work, we should see it through together.

sentences.zh: 然卿觀事勢當有濟理不？

translations.literal: Yet do you survey the situation—is there really a path to success?
translations.idiomatic: But look clear-eyed: is there any realistic chance?

sentences.zh: 敏既常才，本無大略，政令反覆，計無所定，然其子弟各已驕矜，其敗必矣。

translations.literal: Chen Min is merely middling talent, fundamentally lacking great strategy; his orders swing back and forth with no settled plan, yet his sons and nephews already swagger—their defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min is mediocre, without grand design; his policies lurch without fixity while his relatives grow arrogant—the fall is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 而吾等安然受其官祿，事敗之日，使江西諸軍函首送洛，題曰逆賊顧榮、甘卓之首，豈惟一身顛覆，辱及萬世，可不圖之！

translations.literal: Yet we quietly accept his salaries; when the enterprise fails, the Jiangxi armies will box our heads for Luoyang labeled "the traitors Gu Rong and Gan Zhuo"—would that not ruin not only ourselves but shame ten thousand generations? Must we not plan!
translations.idiomatic: Yet we draw his pay in silence; when he collapses, western armies will ship our heads north stamped "rebel chiefs Gu Rong and Gan Zhuo"—destroying us and our memories forever unless we act now!

sentences.zh: 」卓從之。

translations.literal: " Zhuo followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，周圮與榮及甘卓、紀瞻潛謀起兵攻敏。

translations.literal: The next year Zhou Qi joined Rong, Gan Zhuo, and Ji Zhan in secretly plotting to raise troops against Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhou Qi, Gu Rong, Gan Zhuo, and Ji Zhan conspired to strike Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 榮廢橋斂舟于南岸，敏率萬餘人出，不獲濟，榮麾以羽扇，其眾潰散。

translations.literal: Rong dismantled the bridge and gathered boats on the south bank; Chen Min led over ten thousand men out but could not cross; Rong waved a feather fan and his host melted away.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong broke the bridge and massed boats on the southern shore; Chen Min marched out ten thousand strong yet could not ford; Gu Rong merely fluttered a feather fan and the army scattered.

sentences.zh: 事平，還吳。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Peace restored, he went back to Wu.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，徵拜侍中，行至彭城，見禍難方作，遂輕舟而還，語在《紀瞻傳》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongjia era he was summoned as palace attendant; reaching Pengcheng, he saw calamity brewing and took a light boat home, as related in Ji Zhan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongjia he was recalled as palace attendant; at Pengcheng he saw disaster forming, slipped away by swift boat, and returned south—the tale is told in Ji Zhan's memoir.

sentences.zh: 元帝鎮江東，以榮為軍司，加散騎常侍，凡所謀畫，皆以諮焉。

translations.literal: When the Yuan emperor governed east of the river, he appointed Rong army director, added serving attendant-in-ordinary, and consulted him on every plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Langye, later Yuan emperor, made Gu Rong director of the army with concurrent serving attendant-in-ordinary and sought his counsel on all strategy.

sentences.zh: 榮既南州望士，躬處右職，朝野甚推敬之。

translations.literal: Rong, a leading scholar of the southern provinces holding a senior post, was deeply respected at court and in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: As the premier southern gentleman in a weighty office, Gu Rong commanded wide reverence.

sentences.zh: 時帝所幸鄭貴嬪有疾，以祈禱頗廢萬機，榮上箋諫曰：「昔文王父子兄弟乃有三聖，可謂窮理者也。

translations.literal: At that time the honored concubine Lady Zheng, whom the emperor favored, was ill; prayer observances had largely suspended myriad affairs of state, and Rong submitted a remonstrance: "Of old King Wen and his sons and brothers numbered three sages—men who exhausted principle.
translations.idiomatic: The favorite Lady Zheng lay ill, and the sovereign's round of prayers had nearly halted governance; Gu Rong memorialized, "Even King Wen's house counted three sages who plumbed the Way.

sentences.zh: 而文王日昃不暇食，周公一沐三握發，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet King Wen at sundown had no leisure to eat, and the Duke of Zhou broke off three hair-washings—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet King Wen skipped meals at dusk, and the Duke of Zhou thrice released a half-washed coil—why was that?

sentences.zh: 誠以一日萬機，不可不理；

translations.literal: Truly because myriad affairs of a single day cannot go unmanaged;
translations.idiomatic: Because the business of a single court day tolerates no neglect;

sentences.zh: 一言蹉跌，患必及之故也。

translations.literal: one slip of speech brings calamity in its train.
translations.idiomatic: a single misstep draws disaster upon you.

sentences.zh: 當今衰季之末，屬亂離之運，而天子流播，豺狼塞路，公宜露營野次，星言夙駕，伏軾怒蛙以募勇士，懸膽於庭以表辛苦。

translations.literal: In this late age of decay, amid the fortune of chaos and separation, while the Son of Heaven wanders in exile and wolves block the roads, you ought to camp in the open and ride before dawn, lean from your chariot to honor angry frogs and recruit warriors, hang your gall in the hall to display hardship.
translations.idiomatic: We live in collapse: the throne wanders, traitors choke the roads—you should bivouac under stars, ride out at cockcrow, humble yourself like Goujian rallying fighters, and hang your bitter gall where all may see your resolve.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪未安，藥石實急；

translations.literal: The honored concubine is not yet safe—medicine is desperately urgent;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng still hovers between life and death—her physic cannot wait;

sentences.zh: 禱祀之事，誠復可修；

translations.literal: matters of prayer may indeed be pursued;
translations.idiomatic: supplications may continue in due course;

sentences.zh: 豈有便塞參佐白事，斷賓客問訊？

translations.literal: how can you block aides from reporting business or cut off guests' inquiries?
translations.idiomatic: but blocking staff memorials and shutting out visitors is no way to rule.

sentences.zh: 今強賊臨境，流言滿國，人心萬端，去就紛紜。

translations.literal: Now powerful rebels press the borders and rumor fills the realm; ten thousand hearts waver in their choices.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy hosts crowd the frontier and gossip floods the state; loyalty teeters everywhere.

sentences.zh: 願沖虛納下，廣延俊彥，思畫今日之要，塞鬼道淫祀，弘九合之勤，雪天下之恥，則群生有賴，開泰有期矣。」

translations.literal: We hope you will embrace humility, heed subordinates, widen recruitment of worthies, ponder the essentials of today, shut off ghostly byways and excessive cults, revive the diligence of the nine alliances, and wipe away the realm's shame—then the masses will have something to rely on and an age of renewal may dawn."
translations.idiomatic: I pray you open your mind to counsel, summon talent broadly, focus on practical priorities, curb superstitious cults, emulate the steadfast leagues of old, and cleanse our national shame—only then will the people find footing and peace return."

sentences.zh: 時南土之士未盡才用，榮又言：「陸士光貞正清貴，金玉其質；

translations.literal: Because southern scholars had not all been employed to capacity, Rong also said, "Lu Shiguang is upright, pure, and noble—gold and jade are his substance;
translations.idiomatic: Southern talent still languished unused, so Gu Rong added, "Lu Ye is principled, lucid, and refined—pure metal and fine jade at the core;

sentences.zh: 甘季思忠款盡誠，膽幹殊快；

translations.literal: Gan Jisi is devoted and utterly sincere, courageous and decisive;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo is loyal to the bone and strikingly resolute;

sentences.zh: 殷慶元質略有明規，文武可施用；

translations.literal: Yin Qingyuan's substance is measured and his insight reliable—fit for civil and military employ;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Qingyuan pairs steady judgment with usable strength in both brush and blade;

sentences.zh: 榮族兄公讓明亮守節，困不易操；

translations.literal: Rong's elder cousin Gongrang is bright, principled, and unyielding in adversity;
translations.idiomatic: my kinsman Gongrang shines with integrity that hardship cannot bend;

sentences.zh: 會稽楊彥明、謝行言皆服膺儒教，足為公望；

translations.literal: Yang Yanming of Kuaiji and Xie Xingyan are steeped in Confucian teaching—sufficient to stand as your public face;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanming of Kuaiji and Xie Xingyan embody Confucian learning fit for your front rank;

sentences.zh: 賀生沈潛，青雲之士；

translations.literal: Mr. He is deep and still—a man destined for high emoluments;
translations.idiomatic: He Xun moves in quiet depth, a man bound for high appointment;

sentences.zh: 陶恭兄弟才幹雖少，實事極佳。

translations.literal: though the Tao brothers' talents are modest, they are thoroughly reliable in practical duty.
translations.idiomatic: the Tao brothers bring modest gifts yet excel at dependable execution.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸人，皆南金也。

translations.literal: All these men are southern gold.
translations.idiomatic: Each is southern gold ready for the mint.

translations.literal: Later, nominated advanced scholar, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Lu Ji examined him: "The enlightened kings of the three dynasties founded grand enterprises; patterns of civilization differed yet their good names agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to "flourishing talent," he faced examination by Lu Ji: "The sage kings of the three ages raised great orders; some prized culture, others simplicity, yet each earned an impeccable name.

sentences.zh: 然夏人尚忠，忠之弊也朴，救朴莫若敬。

translations.literal: Yet the Xia valued devotion; devotion's fault is plainness, and to remedy plainness nothing surpasses reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Xia rule cherished steadfast loyalty; its excess was rustic bluntness, cured best by solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 殷人革而修焉，敬之弊也鬼，救鬼莫若文。

translations.literal: The Yin reformed and cultivated reverence; reverence's fault is ghostliness, and to remedy ghostliness nothing surpasses pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Shang kings refined that reverence; its excess was superstitious awe, cured best by cultured form.

sentences.zh: 周人矯而變焉，文之弊也薄，救薄則又反之於忠。

translations.literal: The Zhou corrected and altered pattern; pattern's fault is shallow slickness, and to remedy shallowness one again turns toward devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou adjusted toward refinement; its excess was brittle elegance, so wise rulers swung back toward substantive loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然則王道之反覆其無一定邪，亦所祖之不同而功業各異也？

translations.literal: If so, does the kingly way cycle without fixed rule, or do differing ancestries yield differing achievements?
translations.idiomatic: Does the royal path therefore wheel endlessly without fixity, or do distinct origins simply produce distinct legacies?

sentences.zh: 自無聖王，人散久矣。

translations.literal: Since there have been no sage kings, the people have long been scattered.
translations.idiomatic: With true sage-kings gone, the populace has drifted apart for ages.

sentences.zh: 三代之損益，百姓之變遷，其故可得而聞邪？

translations.literal: May I hear the reasons for the three dynasties' adjustments and the hundred clans' transformations?
translations.idiomatic: Explain for me how the three dynasties trimmed policy and how common customs shifted in step.

sentences.zh: 今將反古以救其弊，明風以蕩其穢，三代之制將何所從？

translations.literal: Now we intend to return antiquity to cure present faults and clarify customs to wash away filth—which model of the three dynasties should we follow?
translations.idiomatic: If we now revive antiquity to heal decay and broadcast upright fashion to scour vice—which of the three templates fits?

sentences.zh: 太古之化有何異道？

translations.literal: How did the transformation of high antiquity differ in method?
translations.idiomatic: In what way did the governance of deepest antiquity diverge?

sentences.zh: 」瞻對曰：「瞻聞有國有家者，皆欲邁化隆政，以康庶績，垂歌億載，永傳於後。然而俗變事弊，得不隨時，雖經聖哲，無以易也。故忠弊質野，敬失多儀。周鑒二王之弊，崇文以辯等差，而流遁者歸薄而無款誠，款誠之薄，則又反之於忠。三代相循，如水濟火，所謂隨時之義，救弊之術也。羲皇簡樸，無為而化；後聖因承，所務或異。非賢聖之不同，世變使之然耳。今大晉闡元，聖功日隮，承天順時，九有一貫，荒服之君，莫不來同。然而大道既往，人變由久，謂當今之政宜去文存樸，以反其本，則兆庶漸化，太和可致也。」

translations.literal: Ending Lu Ji's question, Ji Zhan replied: "I have heard that whoever possesses a state or a household wishes to advance transformation and elevate governance so as to secure orderly accomplishment, leave songs for a hundred million years, and transmit them forever to posterity. Yet when customs shift and affairs decay, one cannot but follow the times; even through sages and wise men nothing can replace this. Hence when devotion becomes excessive, substance turns rustic; when reverence errs, ritual prolixity multiplies. Zhou, taking warning from the faults of the two prior kings, honored pattern to distinguish ranks, yet those who drifted away returned shallow and without heartfelt sincerity; when sincerity grew thin, they turned again toward devotion. The three dynasties succeeded one another like water quenching fire—this is what is called the meaning of suiting the age and the technique of remedying decay. The age of Fuxi was simple and unadorned, transformed by nonaction; later sages inherited it, and what they pursued sometimes differed. It is not that worthies and sages differed—the age changed and made them so. Now Great Jin opens its primordial enterprise, sage merit mounts daily, obeying Heaven and following the season; the nine domains are unified, and lords of the outer wilds all come to court. Yet the great Way has already receded; men have long been altered by change. I maintain that government today should strip ornament and preserve simplicity to return to the root; then the myriad households will gradually be transformed and supreme harmony can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan answered: rulers who hold land or lineage all want policy that elevates the age and secures lasting praise, yet institutions must move with their times—no sage can freeze them. Loyalty's excess is rustic bluntness; reverence's excess is hollow ritual. The Zhou cycle corrected Xia and Shang as water checks fire: each swing repairs the last flaw. The ancients ruled simply; later kings inherited shifting tasks—difference lies in circumstance, not wisdom. Great Jin now unites the realm, yet long erosion of the Way means people have drifted. Ji Zhan argued that present rule should shed literary excess, recover substantive simplicity, and let custom return toward the root—only then can the masses ease toward great peace.

sentences.zh: 又問：「在昔哲王象事備物，明堂所以崇上帝，清廟所以甯祖考，辟雍所以班禮教，太學所以講藝文，此蓋有國之盛典，為幫之大司。

translations.literal: He asked again: "Ancient wise kings matched affairs and supplied implements: the Bright Hall honored High God, the Pure Temple brought peace to ancestors, the Border Academy issued ritual instruction, the Imperial Academy expounded arts and letters—these were a state's great ceremonies and a realm's chief offices.
translations.idiomatic: The examiner pressed on: "Former sages aligned institutions with cosmic pattern: the Bright Hall served Heaven, the solemn temple soothed ancestors, the royal academy spread ritual, the imperial college taught letters—these pillars upheld any throne.

sentences.zh: 亡秦廢學，制度荒闕。

translations.literal: The perished Qin abolished learning and left institutions wastefully empty.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's ruin scrapped schooling and shattered every regulation.

sentences.zh: 諸儒之論，損益異物。

translations.literal: Various scholars' discussions adjust or trim unlike things.
translations.idiomatic: Later masters disputed how to patch the gaps, each arguing different pieces.

sentences.zh: 漢氏遺作，居為異事，而蔡邕《月令》謂之一物。

translations.literal: Han-era institutional survivals came to be treated as disparate matters, yet Cai Yong in his "Monthly Ordinances" calls them a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: What Han bequeathed looked like a patchwork of rites, though Cai Yong's Monthly Ordinances folded the whole complex into one conceptual entity.

sentences.zh: 將何所從？

translations.literal: According to what should one choose?
translations.idiomatic: Which line of authority should the court adopt?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「周制明堂，所以宗其祖以配上帝，敬恭明祀，永光孝道也。其大數有六。古者聖帝明王南面而聽政，其六則以明堂為主。又其正中，皆云太廟，以順天時，施行法令，宗祀養老，訓學講肄，朝諸侯而選造士，備禮辯物，一教化之由也。故取其宗祀之類，則曰清廟；取其正室之貌，則曰太廟；取其室，則曰太室；取其堂，則曰明堂；取其四門之學，則曰太學；取其周水圜如璧，則曰璧雍。異名同事，其實一也。是以蔡邕謂之一物。」

translations.literal: Ji Zhan replied: "The Zhou Bright Hall system uses it to honor the ancestor who mates with High God, performing reverent bright sacrifices so filial duty shines forever. Its great reckoning has six parts. Ancient sage kings faced south to hear government; those six functions took the Bright Hall as chief. At its center they all called it the Grand Temple: thereby aligning with heaven's seasons, promulgating commands, performing ancestral rites and elder care, drilling study and lectures, holding audiences with nobles and selecting accomplished men, completing ritual and distinguishing things—the single source of transformation through teaching. Hence for ancestral sacrifice it is called the Pure Temple; for the main chamber's appearance, the Grand Temple; for the chamber itself, the Grand Chamber; for the hall, the Bright Hall; for the four-gate school, the Academy; for the moat round as a jade disk, the Jade-ring Moat. Different names, same task—substantively one. Therefore Cai Yong called them one thing."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan explained Zhou usage: the Bright Hall cluster names one ritual core—honoring ancestors with Heaven, running government, schooling, and audiences—where Pure Temple, Grand Temple, Academy, and round moat are alternate labels for the same institutional heart, which is why Cai Yong spoke of a single thing.

sentences.zh: 又問：「庶明亮采，故時雍穆唐；

translations.literal: Lu Ji asked again: "When commoners displayed shining merit and gathered harvests, therefore the age was harmonious and Tang stood in solemn peace;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji pressed on: when worthy commoners brought brilliance to government, harmony enveloped Yao's Tang.

sentences.zh: 有命既集，而多士隆周。

translations.literal: When the mandate had assembled, many gentlemen raised Zhou to glory.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heaven's charge settled, talented men built Zhou's greatness.

sentences.zh: 故《書》稱明良之歌，《易》貴金蘭之美。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Documents" praises the song of enlightened ministers, and the "Changes" esteems the beauty of bonds like metal and orchid.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents hymns ruler and minister in tune, and the Changes prizes friendships firm as metal and fragrant as orchids.

sentences.zh: 此長世所以廢興，有邦所以崇替。

translations.literal: This is why long reigns rise or fall, why states flourish or fade.
translations.idiomatic: On such ties hang dynastic endurance and the waxing or waning of any realm.

sentences.zh: 夫成功之君勤於求才，立名之士急於招世，理無世不對，而事千載恆背。

translations.literal: Successful rulers labor to seek talent; men who would make a name hurry to answer the age—principle leaves no generation unmatched, yet affairs for a thousand years constantly turn backward.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious kings hunt for helpers; ambitious scholars rush to serve—yet though the logic always fits its day, practice across centuries constantly misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 古之興王何道而如彼？

translations.literal: By what path did ancient rising kings achieve that?
translations.idiomatic: What did founding sovereigns do differently to succeed?

sentences.zh: 後之衰世何闕而如此？

translations.literal: What did later declining ages lack to become like this?
translations.idiomatic: What critical piece did fallen eras refuse to supply?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「興隆之政務在得賢，清平之化急於拔才，故二八登庸，則百揆序；有亂十人，而天下泰。武丁擢傅岩之徒，周文攜渭濱之士，居之上司，委之國政，故能龍奮天衢，垂勳百代。先王身下白屋，搜揚仄陋，使山無扶蘇之才，野無《伐檀》之詠。是以化厚物感，神祇來應，翔鳳飄颻，甘露豐墜，醴泉吐液，硃草自生，萬物滋茂，日月重光，和氣四塞，大道以成；序君臣之義，敦父子之親，明夫婦之道，別長幼之宜，自九州，被八荒，海外移心，重譯入貢，頌聲穆穆，南面垂拱也。今貢賢之途已闓，而教學之務未廣，是以進競之志恆銳，而務學之心不修。若辟四門以延造士，宣五教以明令德，考績殿最，審其優劣，厝之百僚，置之群司，使調物度宜，節宣國典，必協濟康哉，符契往代，明良來應，金蘭復存也。」

translations.literal: Ji Zhan replied: "Flourishing government hinges on obtaining worthies; peaceful transformation urgently promotes talent. Hence when the Eight arose to office, the hundred portfolios fell in order; with ten men against chaos, all under heaven was tranquil. Wu Ding raised men from the cliffs of Fu; King Wen brought scholars from the Wei banks, seated them in high posts and entrusted state policy, so they soared along heaven's highway and left merit for a hundred generations. Former kings humbled themselves to hovels, searched humble lanes, until hills held no hidden talent and fields no unmet grievance like the 'Sandalwood' ode. Therefore transformation thickened, things responded, spirits arrived with omens—phoenix wheeling, sweet dew falling thick, sweet springs bubbling, crimson grass sprouting of itself; myriad creatures flourished, sun and moon redoubled radiance, harmonious qi filled the four quarters, and the great Way was realized: ordering lord and minister, thickening father and son, clarifying husband and wife, distinguishing elder and younger, spreading from the nine provinces through eight wilds, moving overseas hearts and doubled-interpreter tribute, until praise sounded softly and the ruler faced south with folded hands. Now roads for presenting talent are open, yet instruction is not wide; ambition for promotion stays keen while zeal for study withers. Open the four gates to welcome scholars, proclaim the five teachings to display shining virtue, grade performance and rank best and worst, place them among ministers and bureaus so they harmonize affairs and adjust statutes—then you will match the cry of 'How grand!', tally with past ages, draw enlightened ministers, and see metal-and-orchid fellowship restored."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan argued that dynastic vigor lives or dies on recruitment: ancient kings combed every lane for advisers, matched talent to heavy posts, and omens followed natural harmony. Today exams invite men but schools languish; hunger for rank outruns discipline. Widen study, test honestly, deploy graduates across offices, and the court could again hear the music of true cooperation.

sentences.zh: 又問：「昔唐虞垂五刑之教，周公明四罪之制，故世歎清問而時歌緝熙。

translations.literal: Lu Ji asked again: "Formerly Tang and Yu handed down instruction in the five punishments; the Duke of Zhou clarified the code for four crimes; therefore the age sighed at lucid inquiry and sang of brilliant peace.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: antiquity paired moral teaching with measured punishment—hence praise for clear justice and songs of good rule.

sentences.zh: 奸宄既殷，法物滋有。

translations.literal: When villainy grew abundant, legal instruments multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: As crime swelled, statutes and gear of justice piled up.

sentences.zh: 叔世崇三辟之文，暴秦加族誅之律，淫刑淪胥，虐濫已甚。

translations.literal: Decaying ages honored the provisions of the three capital statutes; brutal Qin added laws for clan execution—punishments sank through the ranks and cruelty overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Late dynasties inflated criminal codes; Qin layered kin-extinction clauses until torture drowned society.

sentences.zh: 漢魏遵承，因而弗革。

translations.literal: Han and Wei inherited them and therefore did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei carried that baggage forward unchanged.

sentences.zh: 亦由險泰不同，而救世異術，不得已而用之故也。

translations.literal: This likewise follows from peril versus ease differing, and salvation requiring unlike techniques—they could not but use them.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstance, not cruelty for its own sake, kept harsh law alive—each age borrowed what it thought necessary.

sentences.zh: 寬克之中，將何立而可？

translations.literal: Between lenience and restraint, what foundation should one establish?
translations.idiomatic: Balancing mercy and control, where should the state plant its footing?

sentences.zh: 族誅之法足為永制與不？

translations.literal: Are laws of clan execution sufficient to serve as perpetual statute?
translations.idiomatic: Can wholesale kin punishment ever be a lasting baseline?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「二儀分則兆庶生，兆庶生則利害作。利害之作，有由而然也。太古之時，化道德之教，賤勇力而貴仁義。仁義貴則強不陵弱，眾不暴寡。三皇結繩而天下泰，非惟象刑緝熙而已也。且太古知法，所以遠獄。及其末，不失有罪，是以獄用彌繁，而人彌暴，法令滋章，盜賊多有。《書》曰：『惟敬五刑，以成三德。』叔世道衰，既興三辟，而文公之弊，又加族誅，淫刑淪胥，感傷和氣，化染後代，不能變改。故漢祖指麾而六合回應，魏承漢末，因而未革，將以俗變由久，權時之宜也。今四海一統，人思反本，漸尚簡樸，則貪夫不競；尊賢黜否，則不仁者遠。爾則斟參夷之刑，除族誅之律，品物各順其生，緝熙異世而偕也。」

translations.literal: Ji Zhan replied: "When the two modalities divide, the myriad masses are born; when they are born, benefit and harm arise; benefit and harm spring from causes. In highest antiquity moral transformation was taught, bravery was cheap and benevolence dear—when benevolence was prized the strong did not bully the weak nor crowds assault the few. The Three Sovereigns knotted cords and all under heaven was peaceful—not only because punishments were pictured and brilliant. Moreover earliest ages understood law to keep prisons distant; by their end none escaped guilt, so litigation multiplied, people grew violent, statutes proliferated, and bandits abounded. The Documents says, 'Revere the five punishments to complete the three virtues.' In decadent ages the three capital statutes arose; Duke Wen's faults added clan execution—punishments sank through the ranks, wounded harmonious qi, stained later generations, and could not be altered away. Hence Han's founder waved his arm and the realm answered; Wei inherited Han's end and followed suit, reckoning long habit required temporary expedients. Now the four seas are one and minds yearn for the root; gradually honor simplicity and grasping men will not compete; honor worthies and dismiss the unfit and the cruel will stay distant. Then weigh reducing the 'three-ŭ' penalties and abolishing clan-extinction codes—let each thing follow its life, and brilliant peace may span ages yet differ in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan traced how moral teaching yielded to ever-thicker criminal codes until Han and Wei froze Qin's harshness as fait accompli. With unity restored, he urged peeling back kin-extinction excess and letting simpler virtue curb greed—law should nurture life, not multiply terror.

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「夫五行迭代，陰陽相須，二儀所以隗育，四時所以化生。

translations.literal: Lu Ji asked further: "The five phases succeed one another; yin and yang depend on each other—thereby the two modalities nurture growth and the four seasons transform and generate life.
translations.idiomatic: Another prompt: the Five Agents cycle; yin-yang mutual need feeds heaven and earth and spins the seasons.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱『在天成象，在地成形』。

translations.literal: The "Changes" says, 'Forms complete above in heaven; shapes settle below on earth.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes teaches images aloft and forms below.

sentences.zh: 形象之作，相須之道也。

translations.literal: Shaping images is the way of mutual dependence.
translations.idiomatic: Manifestation is inherently a paired process.

sentences.zh: 若陰陽不調，則大數不得不否；

translations.literal: If yin and yang fall out of tune, the great reckoning cannot but stall;
translations.idiomatic: When yin-yang slip out of phase, the cosmic tally jams;

sentences.zh: 一氣偏廢，則萬物不得獨成。

translations.literal: when any single qi is crippled, myriad things cannot complete alone.
translations.idiomatic: cripple one vital breath and nothing ripens on its own.

sentences.zh: 此應同之至驗，不偏之明證也。

translations.literal: This is the clearest proof of resonance and the unbiased verification of parity.
translations.idiomatic: Nature's chorus and cosmic balance both testify to that mutuality.

sentences.zh: 今有溫泉而無寒火，其故何也？

translations.literal: Today there are warm springs yet no cold fire—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Warm springs abound yet no 'cold fire' twin appears—why should that be?

sentences.zh: 思聞辯之，以釋不同之理。

translations.literal: I wish to hear it argued through to release this inconsistent principle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji asked him to spell out the logic and settle the paradox.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「蓋聞陰陽升降，山澤通氣，初九純卦，潛龍勿用，泉源所托，其溫宜也。若夫水潤下，火炎上，剛柔燥濕，自然之性，故陽動而外，陰靜而內。內性柔弱，以含容為質；外動剛直，以外接為用。是以金水之明內鑒，火日之光外輝，剛施柔受，陽勝陰伏。水之受溫，含容之性也。」

translations.literal: Ji Zhan replied: "I have heard that yin and yang ascend and descend and hills and marshes exchange breath; in the pure first line's hexagram the hidden dragon should not yet act—the spring's resting place naturally tends warm. Water trends downward, fire flames upward; hardness and softness, dryness and dampness are innate natures, hence yang moves outside while yin rests within. Inner nature is supple and takes containment as substance; outer motion is rigid and takes outward contact as function. Thus metal and water shine inwardly while fire and sun blaze outward; hardness deploys, softness receives, yang prevails and yin submits. Water accepting warmth follows the nature of containment."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan framed springs as yin-yang exchange in classical terms: rising qi meets receptive earth-water, so warmth pools without needing a yang 'cold fire' twin—each element behaves by kind.

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「夫窮神知化，才之盡稱；

translations.literal: Lu Ji asked further: "To exhaust spirit and know transformation is the utmost title for talent;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji continued: plumbing mystery and flux exhausts what we call genius;

sentences.zh: 備物致用，功之極目。

translations.literal: to supply implements and extend use is the fullest reach of merit.
translations.idiomatic: stocking tools and putting them to work exhausts what we call practical achievement.

sentences.zh: 以之為政，則黃羲之規可踵；

translations.literal: Employ that in government and the norms of Huang and Xi can be trodden again;
translations.idiomatic: Apply it to rule and you approach the Yellow Emperor's model;

sentences.zh: 以之革亂，則玄古之風可紹。

translations.literal: employ it to reform chaos and winds of deepest antiquity can be continued.
translations.idiomatic: apply it against turmoil and primordial simplicity returns.

sentences.zh: 然而唐虞密皇人之闊綱，夏殷繁帝者之約法，機心起而日進，淳德往而莫返。

translations.literal: Yet Tang and Yu tightened the vast net of the supreme man; Xia and Yin multiplied the terse statutes of emperors—clever minds advanced daily while plain virtue slipped away never to return.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Tang-Yu laws grew intricate while Xia-Shang multiplied skeletal codes—craft multiplied as rustic virtue ebbed.

sentences.zh: 豈太樸一離，理不可振，將聖人之道稍有降殺邪？

translations.literal: Is it that once great simplicity departs principle cannot be revived, or that the Way of sages slightly declines by degrees?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji wondered whether simplicity lost can never return or whether sage teaching itself grades downward.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「政因時以興，機隨物而動，故聖王究窮通之源，審始終之理，適時之宜，期於濟世。皇代質樸，禍難不作，結繩為信，人知所守。大道既離，智惠擾物，夷險不同，否泰異數，故唐虞密皇人之綱，夏殷繁帝者之法，皆廢興有由，輕重以節，此窮神之道，知化之術，隨時之宜，非有降殺也。」

translations.literal: Ji Zhan replied: "Government rises according to the age; expedients move with things—therefore sage kings exhaust the sources of blockage and smooth passage, discern beginning and end, fit timely expedients, and aim to aid the world. In primal royal ages substance was plain, calamity did not arise, knotted cords served as trust, and people knew what to guard. Once the great Way departed, cleverness disturbed things; danger and ease diverged, blockage and openness counted differently—hence Tang and Yu tightened supreme nets while Xia and Yin elaborated imperial codes; each rise and fall had cause, weight measured by degree. This is the way to exhaust spirit, know transformation, and suit the hour—not a graduated decline of sageness."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan answered that institutions thicken as complexity grows, not because sages weaken—each revision answers fresh peril, matching the Changes' ideal of timely change.

sentences.zh: 永康初，州又舉寒素，大司馬辟東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongkang the province again nominated him as humble scholar of plain virtue; the grand marshal summoned him as libationer of the eastern pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongkang's opening year another provincial nomination reached him as a 'cold-placket' scholar, and the grand marshal appointed him eastern-pavilion libationer.

sentences.zh: 其年，除鄢陵公國相，不之官。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed minister of the Principality of Yanling but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The same year brought nomination as Yanling princedom chancellor, which he never assumed.

sentences.zh: 明年，左降松滋侯相。

translations.literal: The next year he was demoted to minister of the Marquisate of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was relegated to administrator of the Songzi marquisate.

sentences.zh: 太安中，棄官歸家，與顧榮等共誅陳敏，語在榮傳。

translations.literal: During Taian he resigned office and returned home, joining Gu Rong and others in executing Chen Min—the account is in Gu Rong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Taian he quit service, went home, and helped Gu Rong eliminate Chen Min, as told in Gu Rong's memoir.

sentences.zh: 召拜尚書郎，與榮同赴洛，在途共論《易》太極。

translations.literal: He was summoned as gentleman of the Masters of Writing and accompanied Gu Rong toward Luoyang; on the road they debated the Supreme Ultimate in the "Changes."
translations.idiomatic: A capital summons made him secretary colleague to Gu Rong; riding north they argued cosmology from the Changes.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「太極者，蓋謂混沌之時曚昧未分，日月含其輝，八卦隱其神，天地混其體，聖人藏其身。

translations.literal: Gu Rong said: "Supreme Ultimate denotes the age of chaos still darkly undivided—sun and moon hoarded radiance within, the eight trigrams hid their spirit, heaven and earth shared one substance, sages concealed themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong opened: Taiji names the twilight state before separation—luminaries, trigrams, cosmos, and sages still folded together.

sentences.zh: 然後廓然既變，清濁乃陳，二儀著象，陰陽交泰，萬物始萌，六合闓拓。

translations.literal: Then suddenly transformation cleared: muddy and pure separated, the two modalities showed their images, yin and yang crossed in harmony, myriad things began to sprout, and the six directions opened wide.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity followed: turbid and clear parted, Heaven and Earth took shape, yin-yang coupled, life stirred, and space unfolded.

sentences.zh: 《老子》云『有物混成，先天地生』，誠《易》之太極也。

translations.literal: The "Laozi" says 'there is a thing confusedly formed, born before heaven and earth'—truthfully that is the Changes' Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi's "murky thing before Heaven and Earth" matches what the Changes calls Taiji.

sentences.zh: 而王氏云『太極天地』，愚謂末當。

translations.literal: Yet Wang Bi calls 'Supreme Ultimate heaven and earth'—I deem that inaccurate.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected Wang Bi's gloss equating Taiji directly with heaven-and-earth.

sentences.zh: 夫兩儀之謂，以體為稱，則是天地；

translations.literal: Speaking of the two modalities by substance names heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Taken as concrete entities, the dyad means Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 以氣為名，則名陰陽。

translations.literal: speaking by qi names them yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: taken as pneuma they are yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 今若謂太極為天地，則是天地自生，無生天地者也。

translations.literal: Now if Supreme Ultimate were heaven and earth, heaven and earth would self-generate with nothing generating heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Equating Taiji to sky and soil implies they arise alone—with no prior principle begetting them.

sentences.zh: 《老子》又云『天地所以能長且久者，以其不自生，故能長久』、『一生二，二生三，三生萬物』，以資始沖氣以為和。

translations.literal: The "Laozi" also says 'Heaven and earth endure long because they do not live for themselves' and 'one births two, two births three, three births myriad things,' harmonizing by nourishing primal qi from the source.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi ties longevity to selfless cycling and counts one-two-three emanations—anchoring genesis in original breath.

sentences.zh: 原元氣之本，求天地之根，恐宜以此為准也。

translations.literal: Tracing primal qi's root and heaven-earth's foundation, we ought to take this as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing yuanqi and cosmic roots, Gu Rong held Laozi's sequence the reliable gauge.

sentences.zh: 」瞻曰：「」榮遂止。

translations.literal: " Ji Zhan said nothing further, and Gu Rong let the matter rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan offered no counterargument, so Gu Rong dropped the debate.

sentences.zh: 至徐州，聞亂日甚，將不行。

translations.literal: Reaching Xuzhou, he heard chaos worsening daily and planned not to continue.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou news of spreading turmoil convinced him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 會刺史裴盾得東海王越書，若榮等顧望，以軍禮發遣，乃與榮及陸玩等各解船棄車牛，一日一夜行三百里，得還揚州。

translations.literal: When Governor Pei Dun received a letter from Prince Donghai Yue—if Gu Rong and company hesitated, they were to be sent off under military orders—thereupon he with Gu Rong, Lu Wan, and others cast off boats, abandoned carts and oxen, covered three hundred li in one day and night, and regained Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Pei Dun enforced Sima Yue's order to hustle waverers onward; Ji Zhan, Gu Rong, and Lu Wan shed conveyances and raced home to Yangzhou in a forced march.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，引為軍諮祭酒，轉鎮東長史。

translations.literal: When the Yuan emperor was general pacifying the east, he summoned Ji Zhan as army advisory libationer, then transferred him to chief clerk pacifying the east.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Langye held the eastern pacification command, he named Ji Zhan army advisory libationer and soon chief clerk on the pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 帝親幸瞻宅，與之同乘而歸。

translations.literal: The emperor personally visited Ji Zhan's house and rode back in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rode to Ji Zhan's door and shared his carriage homeward.

sentences.zh: 以討周馥、華軼功，封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigning against Zhou Fu and Hua Yi he was enfeoffed as marquis of Dou Township.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing Zhou Fu and Hua Yi earned him the Dou township marquisate.

sentences.zh: 石勒入寇，加揚威將軍、都督京口以南至蕪湖諸軍事，以距勒。

translations.literal: When Shi Le invaded he was promoted general inspiring might and area commander from Jingkou south to Wuhu to resist Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's raid brought him the Inspiring Might generalcy with command from Jingkou south to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 勒退，除會稽內史。

translations.literal: When Le withdrew he was appointed interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Le pulled back he became Kuaiji's interior administrator.

sentences.zh: 時有詐作大將軍府符收諸暨令，令已受拘，瞻覺其詐，便破檻出之，訊問使者，果伏詐妄。

translations.literal: Someone forged a grand general's warrant to seize the magistrate of Zhuji; the magistrate was already imprisoned when Ji Zhan sensed fraud, smashed the cage to free him, questioned the courier, and the man confessed deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Forgeries posing as the grand general's office targeted Zhuji's magistrate; Ji Zhan broke him out, interrogated the messenger, and exposed the sham.

sentences.zh: 尋遷丞相軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted army advisory libationer to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he rose to chancellor's army advisory libationer.

sentences.zh: 論討陳敏功，封臨湘縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit in the Chen Min campaign he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: His role against Chen Min brought the Linxiang county marquisate.

sentences.zh: 西臺除侍中，不就。

translations.literal: The western court appointed him palace attendant; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an offered palace attendant; he declined to go.

sentences.zh: 及長安不守，與王導俱入勸進。

translations.literal: When Chang'an fell he entered court with Wang Dao to urge the prince to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After the western capital collapsed he and Wang Dao pressed the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「陛下性與天道，猶復役機神於史籍，觀古人之成敗，今世事舉目可知，不為難見。二帝失禦，宗廟虛廢，神器去晉，於今二載，梓宮未殯，人神失御。陛下膺錄受圖，特天所授。使六合革面，遐荒來庭，宗廟既建，神主復安，億兆向風，殊俗畢至，若列宿之綰北極，百川之歸巨海，而猶欲守匹夫之謙，非所以闡七廟，隆中興也。但國賊宜誅，當以此屈己謝天下耳。而欲逆天時，違人事，失地利，三者一去，雖復傾匡於將來，豈得救祖宗之危急哉！適時之宜萬端，其可綱維大業者，惟理與當。晉祚屯否，理盡於今。促之則得，可以隆中興之祚；縱之則失，所以資奸寇之權：此所謂理也。陛下身當厄運，纂承帝緒，顧望宗室，誰復與讓！當承大位，此所謂當也。四祖廓開宇宙，大業如此。今五都燔爇，宗廟無主，劉載竊弄神器于西北，陛下方欲高讓于東南，此所謂揖讓而救火也。臣等區區，尚所不許，況大人與天地合德，日月並明，而可以失機後時哉！」帝猶不許，使殿中將軍韓績撤去御坐。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan declared: "Your Majesty's nature partakes of Heaven's Way, yet still you drain spirit on histories and study ancient rise and fall—today's situation is plain at a glance, hardly obscure. Two emperors lost the reins; ancestral temples stand empty; the sacred regalia has left Jin these two years; imperial coffins lie unburied; men and gods lack a rider. Your Majesty has received the registers and charts Heaven singled out. You have turned the realm's faces, drawn distant wilds to court, rebuilt temples and stabilized spirit tablets—myriad households face your wind and alien customs arrive like stars looping the Pole Star or rivers pouring into the sea—yet you cling to commoner modesty, not the way to exalt seven temples and elevate restoration. Only state traitors deserve humbling apology to the realm. To oppose heaven's season, human affairs, and earthly advantage—lose any one though you overturn the realm later, how will you save our ancestors' peril? Among myriad timely measures what steadies great enterprise is principle and fitness to circumstance. Jin's fortune stands blocked; principle is exhausted now—press forward and you lengthen restoration; drag heels and you feed usurpers: that is principle. Your Majesty inherits fate amid crisis—scan the imperial clan: who else yields? You must accept the great seat: that is fitness. Four ancestors carved out this cosmos; now five capitals burn, temples lack masters, Liu Zai toys with the regalia in the northwest while Your Majesty plays lofty yielding in the southeast—this is bowing politely while the house burns. We petty ministers cannot endorse it; how less one whose virtue mates heaven and earth and shines like sun and moon—may you miss the hour!" Still the emperor refused and ordered palace general Han Ji to remove the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan's memorial insisted heaven, history, and the ruined western throne all compelled the prince to accept—the empire already rallied to him while Liu Zai seized Chang'an; further refusal was courteous folly. The sovereign still balked and told guards to strip the throne dais.

sentences.zh: 瞻叱績曰：「帝坐上應星宿，敢有動者斬！

translations.literal: Ji Zhan rebuked Ji: "The emperor's seat aligns with astral mansions—whoever dares move it dies!
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan roared at Han Ji that the throne answered constellations—touch it and die.

sentences.zh: 」帝為之改容。

translations.literal: " The emperor's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's face shifted at that.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐位，拜侍中，轉尚書，上疏諫諍，多所匡益，帝甚嘉其忠烈。

translations.literal: When the emperor assumed the throne Ji Zhan was appointed palace attendant, transferred to president of the Masters of Writing; his memorials remonstrated often and greatly aided rule—the emperor praised his fierce loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the ruler made him attendant-in-ordinary, then chief secretary; his blunt papers corrected policy and won deep praise.

sentences.zh: 會久疾，不堪朝請，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Because chronic illness kept him from court audiences he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Long sickness barred court attendance, so he forwarded a petition opening:

sentences.zh: 臣疾疢不痊，曠廢轉久，比陳誠款，未見哀察。重以屍素，抱罪枕席，憂責之重，不知垂沒之餘當所投厝。臣聞易失者時，不再者年，故古之志士義人負鼎趣走，商歌於市，誠欲及時效其忠規，名傳不朽也。然失之者億萬，得之者一兩耳。常人之情，貪求榮利。臣以凡庸，邂逅遭遇，勞無負鼎，口不商歌，橫逢大運，頻煩饕竊。雖思慕古人自效之志，竟無毫釐報塞之效，而犬馬齒衰，眾疾廢頓，僵臥救命，百有餘日，叩棺曳衾，日頓一日。如復天假之年，蒙陛下行葦之惠，適可薄存性命，枕息陋巷，亦無由復廁八坐，升降臺閣也。臣目冥齒墮，胸腹冰冷，創既不差，足復偏跛，為病受困，既以荼毒。七十之年，禮典所遺，衰老之徵，皎然露見。臣雖欲勤自藏護，隱伏何地！ 臣之職掌，戶口租稅，國之所重。方今六合波蕩，人未安居，始被大化，百度草創，發卒轉運，皆須人力。以臣平強，兼以晨夜，尚不及事，今俟命漏刻，而當久停機職，使王事有廢。若朝廷以之廣恩，則憂責日重；以之序官，則官廢事弊；須臣差，則臣日月衰退。今以天慈，使官曠事滯，臣受偏私之宥，於大望亦有虧損。

translations.literal: Your servant's illness does not heal; absence drags on; repeated earnest pleas drew no compassionate notice. Added to corpse-like incompetence I lie guilty on the mat—the weight of worry leaves no idea where to lodge these dying days. I hear opportunity slips easily and years do not return; hence ancient worthies shouldered cauldrons, hurried markets, and sang peddler songs—desiring timely loyalty and deathless names—yet ten thousand miss while one or two seize the moment. Ordinary minds crave glory; I am vulgar and stumbled into fortune without cauldron labor or street song yet repeatedly stole heavy posts. Though I long to emulate ancient devotion I repay nothing; horse-teeth fade, ailments cripple me a hundred days abed coffin-bound, worsening daily. Even years borrowed with your reed-sheaf kindness would barely preserve breath in a humble lane—never again mount the Eight Seats or palace stairs. Eyes dim, teeth fall, chest and belly ice-cold; wounds fester, legs lame—affliction tortures me past seventy, ages ritual abandons; decay shows plainly. Though I guard myself, where could I hide? My charge—households, rents, taxes—is what the state weighs most. Now the realm tosses unsettled; people barely shelter under new transformation; every measure is draft; levies and transport need labor. At full strength I raced night and day yet barely kept pace; awaiting dawn audiences while idling critical posts wastes royal business. If court reads this as grace, my burden swells; if as roster order, offices rot waiting while I fade. Imperial kindness now lets posts lie vacant and tasks stall—your servant enjoys partial favor yet the great expectation suffers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan begged leave with blunt candor: his chronic sickness and advancing age—past the ritual age of release—left him unfit for revenue portfolios while the realm still shook from war; holding the post only paralyzed household registration and tax work, stacked shame on a hollow appointee, and blocked younger men who could actually run the machinery of state.

sentences.zh: 今萬國革面，賢俊比跡，而當虛停好爵，不以縻賢，以臣穢病之餘，妨官固職，誠非古今黜進之急。惟陛下割不已之仁，賜以敝帷，隕僕之日，得以藉屍；時銓俊乂，使官修事舉，臣免罪戮，死生厚幸！

translations.literal: Now myriad states turn anew and worthies crowd forward—yet prize ranks idle unrewarded while my sick frame blocks efficient posts—hardly the urgent lesson of promotion and demotion through the ages. May Your Majesty cut endless mercy, grant a worn curtain so when I fall I may cover my corpse; timely elevate heroes so offices run and affairs lift—spare me shame and execution; life or death would be fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to step aside so healthier men could fill elite posts—asking only a modest burial cloth and an orderly replacement.

sentences.zh: 因以疾免。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was relieved on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he retired sick.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書右僕射，屢辭不聽，遂稱病篤，還第，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed right vice-president of the Masters of Writing; repeated refusals went unheard, so he claimed grave illness and returned home—the court still refused.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately named him right vice-president; he declined repeatedly, feigned collapse at home, yet orders persisted.

sentences.zh: 時郗鑒據鄒山，屢為石勒等所侵逼。

translations.literal: At that time Xi Jian held Zou Mountain and was repeatedly harassed by Shi Le and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian's refuge on Zou Mountain faced repeated pressure from Shi Le's forces.

sentences.zh: 瞻以鑒有將相之材，恐朝廷棄而不恤，上疏請征之，曰：「臣聞皇代之興，必有爪牙之佐，捍城之用，帝王之利器也。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan, deeming Xi Jian possessed ministerial talent and fearing court might abandon him without relief, submitted a memorial urging summons: "I hear every rising age needs claw-and-fang assistants and bulwark officers—the sovereign's keen weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the court would neglect Xi Jian's genius, Ji Zhan argued great regimes always need warrior-ministers at the edges.

sentences.zh: 故虞舜舉十六相而南面垂拱。

translations.literal: Hence Shun raised sixteen ministers and faced south with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu Shun promoted sixteen aides and ruled effortlessly.

sentences.zh: 伏見前輔國將軍郗鑒，少立高操，體清望峻，文武之略，時之良幹。

translations.literal: I bow to former Champion general Xi Jian: in youth he set high integrity; his bearing is lucid, reputation steep, civil and military strategy makes him a pillar of the hour.
translations.idiomatic: He spotlighted Xi Jian—early austerity, sterling name, talent for camp and capital alike.

sentences.zh: 昔與戴若思同辟，推放荒地，所在孤特，眾無一旅，救援不至。

translations.literal: Once nominated with Dai Ruosi he was shoved to wild borderlands, isolated without a full regiment and no rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Banished with Dai Yong to frontier duty, he lacked troops or relief.

sentences.zh: 然能綏集殘餘，據險曆載，遂使凶寇不敢南侵。

translations.literal: Yet he soothed survivors, held rugged terrain for years, and kept fierce raiders from pressing south.
translations.idiomatic: Still he rallied remnants and barred southern invasion for years.

sentences.zh: 但士眾單寡，無以立功，既統名州，又為常伯。

translations.literal: Only troops stayed thin so merit went unrecorded; now he commands a famed province while holding standing attendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: Thin ranks limited glory though he already leads a great province with court standing.

sentences.zh: 若使鑒從容臺闥，出內王命，必能盡抗直之規，補袞職之闕。

translations.literal: Were Xi Jian eased through palace gates to convey royal commands, he would surely offer blunt counsel and plug ministerial gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Bring him inside to relay edicts and he would temper policy with straight speech.

sentences.zh: 自先朝以來，諸所授用，已有成比。

translations.literal: Since the prior reign appointments have followed clear precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Recent reigns set parallel promotions.

sentences.zh: 戴若思以尚書為六州都督、征西將軍，復加常侍，劉隗鎮北，陳眕鎮東。

translations.literal: Dai Ruosi rose from Masters of Writing to six-province commander and expedition-west general plus attendant; Liu Kun guarded the north; Chen Zhen held the east.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yong jumped from secretary to multi-province command; Liu Kun and Chen Zhen held comparable frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 以鑒年時，則與若思同；

translations.literal: Measured by age Xi Jian matches Ruosi;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian's seniority aligns with Dai Yong's;

sentences.zh: 以資，則俱八坐。

translations.literal: measured by pedigree both reached the Eight Seats.
translations.idiomatic: by résumé both earned seats among the eight department heads.

sentences.zh: 況鑒雅望清重，一代名器。

translations.literal: Moreover Xi Jian's repute is weighty—a vessel for an age.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian's stature marks him as generation-defining timber.

sentences.zh: 聖朝以至公臨天下，惟平是與，是以臣寢頓陋巷，思盡聞見，惟開聖懷，垂問臣導，冀有毫釐萬分之一。」

translations.literal: The sacred court judges all under heaven with utmost fairness and admits only balance—therefore your servant, abed in a mean lane, wishes to exhaust what he has heard and only beg an open sacred mind to inquire of minister Wang Dao, hoping for one ten-thousandth acceptance."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan appealed to impartial heaven: consult Wang Dao if need be, but do not strand Xi Jian—grant him a central role proportionate to peers.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘗獨引瞻於廣室，慨然憂天下，曰：「社稷之臣，欲無復十人，如何？

translations.literal: Emperor Ming once drew Ji Zhan alone into a broad chamber, sighed anxiously over the realm, and said: "Pillars of the altars—I fear we lack even ten—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Ming emperor shut Ji Zhan in a side hall and mourned that fewer than ten true pillars seemed left.

sentences.zh: 」因屈指曰：「君便其一。

translations.literal: " Then counting fingers: "You count as one.
translations.idiomatic: Flexing fingers he added, "You are one of them.

sentences.zh: 」瞻辭讓。

translations.literal: " Ji Zhan declined modestly.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan protested the praise.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「方欲與君善語，復云何崇謙讓邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I mean to speak frankly with you—why rehearse excessive modesty!
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign told him to spare empty humility—they needed plain talk.

sentences.zh: 」瞻才兼文武，朝廷稱其忠亮雅正。

translations.literal: " Ji Zhan combined civil and martial gifts; court praised his loyalty, clarity, and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion deemed Ji Zhan loyal, lucid, and upright in civil and military duty.

sentences.zh: 俄轉領軍將軍，當時服其嚴毅。

translations.literal: Soon he shifted to general commanding the guards; contemporaries respected his stern dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to command the palace armies, he impressed all with severity.

sentences.zh: 雖恆疾病，六軍敬憚之。

translations.literal: Though constantly ill the six armies feared and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Even chronically sick he overawed the capital hosts.

sentences.zh: 瞻以久病，請去官，不聽，復加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan, citing long sickness, sought removal; the throne refused and added serving attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to quit; the emperor refused and piled on another concurrent honor.

sentences.zh: 及王敦之逆，帝使謂瞻曰：「卿雖病，但為朕臥護六軍，所益多矣。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled the emperor sent word: "Though you are ill, merely lying to shield the six armies helps me immensely.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Dun's coup the throne begged bedridden Ji Zhan to oversee the armies symbolically.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜布千匹。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was granted a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court awarded a thousand rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 瞻不以歸家，分賞將士。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan did not take them home but divided them among officers.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the silk straight to troops instead of carting it home.

sentences.zh: 賊平，復自表還家，帝不許，固辭不起。

translations.literal: After bandits were crushed he again petitioned to retire; the emperor forbade it; he adamantly declined and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he pressed retirement again—still denied—yet stayed off duty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「瞻忠亮雅正，識局經濟，屢以年耆病久，逡巡告誠。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Ji Zhan is loyal, lucid, and upright, discerning and statesmanlike; repeatedly citing advanced age and lingering illness he hesitates with earnest disclaimers.
translations.idiomatic: The throne acknowledged his repeated pleas—praising his loyalty and grasp of statecraft while noting old age and sickness.

sentences.zh: 朕深明此操，重違高志，今聽所執，其以為驃騎將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: We deeply grasp this integrity yet shrink from thwarting lofty intent—now we heed his resolve: appoint him chief commander while serving attendant-in-ordinary continues as before.
translations.idiomatic: The edict honored his integrity by naming him chief commander yet letting him keep concurrent palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 服物制度，一按舊典。

translations.literal: Robes, gifts, and statutory grades all followed former canons.
translations.idiomatic: Court vestments and precedent matched classical regulation.

sentences.zh: 」遣使就拜，止家為府。

translations.literal: " Envoys were dispatched to invest him at home, treating his residence as headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers carried the commission to his house, which doubled as his command post.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 冊贈本官、開府儀同三司，諡曰穆，遣御史持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: Posthumous patent restored his substantive offices plus privilege opening a separate headquarters matching the Three Offices, posthumous name Mu, and an imperial clerk was sent with baton to supervise mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously stacked honors—chief commander privileges and the epithet Mu—and supervised the funeral by imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 論討王含功，追封華容子，降先爵二等，封次子一人亭侯。

translations.literal: For merit against Wang Han he was retroactively invested as viscount of Huarong, his prior noble rank lowered two grades, and one younger son was enfeoffed village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign credit against Wang Han brought a posthumous viscounty at Huarong while trimming an earlier fief and raising one son to hamlet lord.

sentences.zh: 瞻性靜默，少交遊，好讀書，或手自抄寫，凡所著述，詩賦箋表數十篇。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan was quiet by nature, mingled little, loved books, sometimes copying texts himself; his compositions—poems, rhapsodies, memorials—numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan lived withdrawn, read voraciously, copied manuscripts by hand, and left dozens of polished essays and petitions.

sentences.zh: 兼解音樂，殆盡其妙。

translations.literal: He equally grasped music and plumbed its subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered musical theory to its finest shades.

sentences.zh: 厚自奉養，立宅于烏衣巷，館宇崇麗，園池竹木，有足賞玩焉。

translations.literal: He indulged his household generously, building on Wuyi Lane mansions towering and gardens of bamboo and timber worth savoring.
translations.idiomatic: He funded an opulent compound on Wuyi Lane—lofty halls and landscaped groves.

sentences.zh: 慎行愛士，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Prudent in conduct and cherishing gentlemen, he grew only more earnest with age.
translations.idiomatic: His carriage stayed careful and his patronage of scholars deepened in old age.

sentences.zh: 尚書閔鴻、太常薛兼、廣川太守河南褚沈、給事中宣城章遼、曆陽太守沛國武嘏，並與瞻素疏，咸藉其高義，臨終托後於瞻。

translations.literal: Min Hong of the Masters of Writing, Xue Jian of the Grand Temple, Chu Shen prefect of Guangchuan in Henan, Zhang Liao of Xuancheng among palace presenters, and Wu Gu of Pei as Liyang prefect—all distant acquaintances—relied on his lofty righteousness and entrusted posterity to him as they died.
translations.idiomatic: Diverse officials who barely knew him personally leaned on his integrity to settle estates and heirs.

sentences.zh: 瞻悉營護其家，為起居宅，同於骨肉焉。

translations.literal: Ji Zhan wholly sheltered their families, raised dwellings for them, as though kin.
translations.idiomatic: He housed and fed those families like blood relations.

sentences.zh: 少與陸機兄弟親善，及機被誅，贍恤其家周至，及嫁機女，資送同於所生。

translations.literal: In youth he befriended Lu Ji and his brothers; when Lu Ji was executed he maintained his household generously and, marrying Lu Ji's daughter, supplied dowry equal to a daughter of his own.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Ji's death he kept the Lu household solvent and gave Lu's daughter a wedding as lavish as his own child's.

sentences.zh: 長子景早卒。

translations.literal: Eldest son Jing died young.
translations.idiomatic: His firstborn Jing predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 景子友嗣，官至廷尉。

translations.literal: Jing's son You inherited, reaching the presidency of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson You succeeded him to the chief judgeship.

sentences.zh: 景弟鑒，太子庶子、大將軍從事中郎，先瞻卒。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Jian served as attendant to the heir apparent and gentleman consultant on the grand general's staff, dying before Ji Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Younger son Jian died earlier still, serving the heir and chancellery staff.

sentences.zh: 賀循

translations.literal: He Xun
translations.idiomatic: He Xun

sentences.zh: 賀循，字彥先，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: He Xun, courtesy name Yanxian, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun of Kuaiji bore the style Yanxian.

sentences.zh: 其先慶普，漢世傳《禮》，世所謂慶氏學。

translations.literal: His ancestor Qing Pu transmitted the "Rites" under Han—what the world calls the Qing school.
translations.idiomatic: The clan founder Qing Pu taught the Han Rites tradition remembered as the Qing lineage.

sentences.zh: 族高祖純，博學有重名，漢安帝時為侍中，避安帝父諱，改為賀氏。

translations.literal: Clan forebear Chun was broadly learned and famed; under Han Andi he served as palace attendant and, avoiding the emperor's father's taboo, changed the surname to He.
translations.idiomatic: Forebear He Chun earned court rank until a naming taboo forced the switch from Qing to He.

sentences.zh: 曾祖齊，仕吳為名將。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Qi served Wu as a celebrated general.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qi was a famed Wu commander.

sentences.zh: 祖景，滅賊校尉。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jing was colonel exterminating bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Jing held the bandit-suppression colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 父邵，中書令，為孫皓所殺，徙家屬邊郡。

translations.literal: Father Shao was director of the Palace Secretariat, executed by Sun Hao with kin banished to frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Father He Shao fell to Sun Hao's purge and the family was exiled.

sentences.zh: 循少嬰家難，流放海隅，吳平，乃還本郡。

translations.literal: Xun suffered domestic catastrophe in youth, was banished to the seaside, and only after Wu's fall returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned by Sun Hao's cruelty, he lived in coastal exile until Wu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 操尚高厲，童齔不群，言行進止，必以禮讓，國相丁乂請為五官掾。

translations.literal: His conduct soared high; even as a child he stood apart, every movement grounded in courtesy—the commandery minister Ding Yi recruited him as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was austere and ceremonious; Ding Yi named him senior registrar.

sentences.zh: 刺史嵇喜舉秀才，除陽羨令，以寬惠為本，不求課最。

translations.literal: Inspector Xi Xi nominated him flourishing talent; appointed Yangxian magistrate he prized lenience over chasing top evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xi's nomination brought Yangxian, where he ruled gently rather than chasing inspector rankings.

sentences.zh: 後為武康令，俗多厚葬，及有拘忌回避歲月，停喪不葬者，循皆禁焉。

translations.literal: Later as Wukang magistrate he forbade lavish burials and calendar taboos that left corpses unburied.
translations.idiomatic: At Wukang he outlawed wasteful funerals and astrological excuses that stalled burials.

sentences.zh: 政教大行，鄰城宗之。

translations.literal: Instructions spread widely and neighboring cities modeled themselves on him.
translations.idiomatic: His reforms rippled outward until neighboring seats copied him.

sentences.zh: 然無援於朝，久不進序。

translations.literal: Yet lacking court patrons he long went unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Without capital backing promotion stalled.

sentences.zh: 著作郎陸機上疏薦循曰：「伏見武康令賀循德量邃茂，才鑒清遠，服膺道素，風操凝峻，歷試二城，刑政肅穆。

translations.literal: Secretary Lu Ji memorialized: "I bow to Magistrate He Xun of Wukang—virtue deep as a gorge, judgment lucid and far-seeing, steeped in plain integrity, manner stern; tested in two posts, punishments and edicts stayed orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's petition praised He Xun's moral depth and tidy administration across two counties.

sentences.zh: 前蒸陽令郭訥風度簡曠，器識朗拔，通濟敏悟，才足幹事。

translations.literal: Former Zhengyang magistrate Guo Ne bears open manner, keen judgment, practical wit—talent enough to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He paired the plea with praise for Guo Ne's administrative clarity.

sentences.zh: 循守下縣，編名凡悴；

translations.literal: Xun guards a humble county yet ranks among ordinary talents;
translations.idiomatic: He Xun languishes in a minor seat though worthy of higher trust;

sentences.zh: 訥歸家巷，棲遲有年。

translations.literal: Ne sits idle in his lane, lingering for years.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ne wastes years sidelined at home.

sentences.zh: 皆出自新邦，朝無知己，居在遐外，志不自營，年時倏忽，而邈無階緒，實州党愚智所為恨恨。

translations.literal: Both hail from newly annexed lands, lack court allies, dwell far away, never angle for promotion—years flash past without ladder—sparking regret among wise and foolish alike.
translations.idiomatic: Both are southern newcomers without patrons—time slips while talents idle, frustrating every observer.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏思台郎所以使州，州有人，非徒以均分顯路，惠及外州而已。

translations.literal: We reflect why secretaries dispatch province inspectors: not merely to spread sinecures abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji argued provincial postings exist for more than doling out sinecures.

sentences.zh: 誠以庶士殊風，四方異俗，壅隔之害，遠國益甚。

translations.literal: Truly common scholars follow divergent customs; distant regions suffer worst when blocked from audience.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier customs diverge; isolation hurts distant commands most.

sentences.zh: 至於荊、揚二州，戶各數十萬，今揚州無郎，而荊州江南乃無一人為京城職者，誠非聖朝待四方之本心。

translations.literal: Jing and Yang provinces each hold hundreds of thousands of households—yet Yang lacks secretarial officers and south-of-the-river Jing has none serving the capital—hardly the sacred court's intent toward the quadrants.
translations.idiomatic: He stressed that omitting Yang and Jing men from capital desks betrayed inclusive policy.

sentences.zh: 至於才望資品，循可尚書郎，訥可太子洗馬、舍人。

translations.literal: By talent and résumé Xun fits Masters of Writing gentleman; Ne fits heir-apparent groom or attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun deserved a secretary post; Guo Ne a palace grooming office.

sentences.zh: 此乃眾望所積，非但企及清途，苟充方選也。

translations.literal: This stacks popular expectation—not naked ambition for 'pure' tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion, not selfish craving, demanded these moves.

sentences.zh: 謹條資品，乞蒙簡察。

translations.literal: Respectfully listing qualifications, we beg review.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji closed by begging scrutiny of their dossiers.

sentences.zh: 」久之，召補太子舍人。

translations.literal: " After long delay Xun was summoned as heir-apparent attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually He Xun received heir-attendant appointment.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，轉侍御史，辭疾去職。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped he shifted to attendant censor but pled sickness and quit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun's coup moved him to censorial duty; illness became his excuse to resign.
