sentences.zh: 後除南中郎長史，不就，會逆賊李辰起兵江夏，征鎮不能討，皆望塵奔走。

translations.literal: Later nominated chief clerk to the southern interior general he declined; rebel Li Chen rose in Jiangxia and local commands fled rather than fight.
translations.idiomatic: A southern staff summon went unanswered just as Li Chen's Jiangxia revolt panicked garrison commanders into rout.

sentences.zh: 辰別帥石冰略有揚州，逐會稽相張景，以前寧遠護軍程超代之，以其長史宰與領山陰令。

translations.literal: Chen's lieutenant Shi Bing seized Yangzhou, expelled Kuaiji minister Zhang Jing, installed colonel Cheng Chao in his place, and made clerk Zai Yu acting Shanyin magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bing's faction drove Zhang Jing out and stacked Kuaiji with Cheng Chao and Zai Yu.

sentences.zh: 前南平內史王矩、吳興內史顧秘、前秀才周圮等唱義，傳檄州郡以討之，循亦合眾應之。

translations.literal: Former Nanping interior administrator Wang Ju, Wuxing interior administrator Gu Mi, advanced scholar Zhou Qi and others raised righteousness, circulated proclamations, and Xun likewise rallied troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju, Gu Mi, Zhou Qi, and He Xun answered with coalition armies and league proclamations.

sentences.zh: 冰大將抗寵有眾數千，屯郡講堂。

translations.literal: Bing's general Kang Chong held several thousand men in the commandery lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chong quartered thousands in the county school compound.

sentences.zh: 循移檄於寵，為陳逆順，寵遂遁走，超、與皆降，一郡悉平。

translations.literal: Xun sent Chong a manifesto explaining rebellion versus loyalty; Chong fled, Chao and Yu surrendered, and the commandery quieted.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun's tract persuaded Kang Chong to bolt; Cheng Chao and Zai Yu capitulated.

sentences.zh: 循迎景還郡，即謝遣兵士，杜門不出，論功報賞，一無豫焉。

translations.literal: He welcomed Zhang Jing back, dismissed his soldiers, sealed his gates, and refused every merit reward.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring Zhang Jing, he disbanded levies, stayed home, and spurned honors.

sentences.zh: 及陳敏之亂，詐稱詔書，以循為丹陽內史。

translations.literal: During Chen Min's turmoil forged edicts named Xun Danyang interior administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's forged orders made him Danyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 循辭以腳疾，手不制筆，又服寒食散，露發袒身，示不可用，敏竟不敢逼。

translations.literal: He pled foot ailments, inability to hold a brush, cold-food powder madness, hair loose and torso bare—proving uselessness—until Min dared not force him.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned crippled feet, trembling hands, disheveled cold-powder toxicity until Chen Min backed off.

sentences.zh: 是時州內豪傑皆見維縶，或有老疾，就加秩命，惟循與吳郡硃誕不豫其事。

translations.literal: Meanwhile local heroes were shackled or dragooned even when aged; only Xun and Zhu Dan of Wu escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Elites were impressed everywhere except He Xun and Zhu Dan.

sentences.zh: 及敏破，征東將軍周馥上循領會稽相，尋除吳國內史，公車征賢良，皆不就。

translations.literal: After Min fell eastern expedition general Zhou Fu nominated Xun titular Kuaiji minister, then Wu interior minister; imperial carts summoned worthies—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Chen Min he repeatedly refused Kuaiji and Wu posts plus court summons.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，復上循為吳國內史，與循言及吳時事，因問曰：「孫皓嘗燒鋸截一賀頭，是誰邪？

translations.literal: When Prince of Langye held eastern pacification he again nominated Xun Wu minister and reminisced about Wu times: "Sun Hao once burned saws to cut off a He's head—who was that?
translations.idiomatic: The future Yuan emperor, reopening Wu topics, asked which He Sun Hao had mutilated.

sentences.zh: 」循未及言，帝悟曰：「是賀邵也。

translations.literal: " Before Xun answered the emperor realized: "That was He Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The prince caught himself: the victim was He Shao.

sentences.zh: 」循流涕曰：「先父遭遇無道，循創巨痛深，無以上答。

translations.literal: " Xun wept: "My father suffered a lawless ruler; my wound is too deep for words.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun answered through tears about his father's torture.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚愧之，三日不出。

translations.literal: " The emperor was deeply ashamed and stayed indoors three days.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, the prince secluded himself three days.

sentences.zh: 東海王越命為參軍，徵拜博士，並不起。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai ordered staff posts and doctoral summons—he rose for neither.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue's staff and academy calls went ignored.

sentences.zh: 及帝遷鎮東大將軍，以軍司顧榮卒，引循代之。

translations.literal: When the prince advanced to grand marshal pacifying the east and army director Gu Rong died, He Xun was tapped to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion to eastern marshal after Gu Rong's death targeted He Xun as army director.

sentences.zh: 循稱疾篤，箋疏十餘上。

translations.literal: Xun claimed grave illness and filed over ten memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded terminal sickness in relentless petitions.

sentences.zh: 帝遺之書曰：

translations.literal: The emperor sent him a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince dispatched a personal letter.

sentences.zh: 夫百行不同，故出處道殊，因性而用，各任其真耳。當宇宙清泰，彝倫攸序，隨運所遇，動默在己。或有遐棲高蹈，輕舉絕俗，逍遙養和，恬神自足，斯蓋道隆人逸，勢使其然。若乃時運屯弊，主危國急，義士救時，驅馳拯世，燭之武縋城以入秦，園綺彈冠而匡漢，豈非大雅君子卷舒合道乎！虛薄寡德，忝備近親，謬荷寵位，受任方鎮，餐服玄風，景羨高矩，常願棄結駟之軒軌，策柴篳而造門，徒有其懷，而無從賢之實者何？良以寇逆殷擾，諸夏分崩，皇居失禦，黎元荼毒，是以日夜憂懷，慷慨發憤，志在竭節耳。前者顧公臨朝，深賴高算。元凱既登，巢許獲逸。至於今日，所謂道之云亡，邦國殄悴，群望顒顒，實在君侯。苟義之所在，豈得讓勞居逸！想達者亦一以貫之也。庶稟徽猷，以弘遠規。今上尚書，屈德為軍司，謹遣參軍沈禎銜命奉授，望必屈臨，以副傾遲。

translations.literal: "The hundred conducts differ, hence withdrawal versus office diverges—each follows authentic bent. When all under heaven was bright and ethics aligned, motion or stillness rested with the individual: some climbed beyond the vulgar, nursed harmony, found self-content—that was Way lofty and men at ease. When fate falters and the throne totters, righteous men spur to save the age—Zhu Zhiwu was lowered on ropes into Qin; men of Shang capped themselves to steady Han—is this not how great gentlemen bend with the moment? I am shallow and thinly virtuous, ashamed by kinship yet commanding a province—though I breathe mysterious winds and envy high exemplars I would trade coach splendor to knock at your gate—why zeal without deeds? Because rebels riot, the heartland shatters, the palace loses reins, people groan—I burn from duty night and day. Earlier Duke Gu faced court leaning on your plots; worthies rose while hermits rested. Today they say the Way perishes and the state withers—every eye hangs on you, lord. Where righteousness calls, how indulge ease? The discerning read continuity through change. Accept these counsels to widen far plans. Now we memorialize the Masters of Writing: humble your virtue to army director—we send aide Shen Zhen with mandate—trust you will come and answer desperate longing."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui’s letter argued that times of peace let gentlemen retreat, but collapsed dynasties summon rescuers like Zhu Zhiwu or the Shangshan hermits—modesty was luxury he could no longer afford while rebels shattered the north and every hopeful eye fixed on He Xun; remembering Gu Rong’s reliance on his counsel, he begged him to take the army director’s seal and ride back with Shen Zhen before eastern morale frayed entirely.

sentences.zh: 循猶不起。

translations.literal: Still Xun did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun still refused.

sentences.zh: 及帝承制，復以為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: When the prince assumed provisional authority he again named Xun army advisory libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Under interim rule He Xun became army advisory libationer.

sentences.zh: 循稱疾，敦逼不得已，乃轝疾至。

translations.literal: Xun pled sickness until Wang Dun's pressure forced him carried on a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's coercion finally brought him borne by carrying-chair.

sentences.zh: 帝親幸其舟，因諮以政道。

translations.literal: The emperor visited his boat and consulted governance.
translations.idiomatic: The prince boarded his vessel for policy talk.

sentences.zh: 循羸疾不拜謁，乃就加朝服，賜第一區，車馬床帳衣褥等物。

translations.literal: Enfeebled he could not bow; they draped court dress on him and granted a mansion, horses, beds, hangings, bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Too weak for court bows, he received investiture robes plus house and equipage.

sentences.zh: 循辭讓，一無所受。

translations.literal: He declined everything.
translations.idiomatic: He refused each gift.

sentences.zh: 廷尉張闓住在小市，將奪左右近宅以廣其居，乃私作都門，早閉晏開，人多患之，論於州府，皆不見省。

translations.literal: Commandant of justice Zhang Kai dwelt in the market quarter, plotting to seize neighboring homes for expansion; he privately built a ward gate closing early and opening late—neighbors complained to authorities without redress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai bullied neighbors with illegal gates until lawsuits failed.

sentences.zh: 會循出，至破岡，連名詣循質之。

translations.literal: When Xun traveled to Broken Ridge joint plaintiffs appealed.
translations.idiomatic: At Pokang petitioners cornered him.

sentences.zh: 循曰：「見張廷尉，當為言及之。

translations.literal: Xun said: "Seeing Commandant Zhang I shall mention it.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun promised to speak with Zhang Kai.

sentences.zh: 」闓聞而遽毀其門，詣循致謝。

translations.literal: " Kai hearing hastily demolished his gate and apologized to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai tore down the gate and apologized.

sentences.zh: 其為世所敬服如此。

translations.literal: Such was the awe he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that degree of public respect.

sentences.zh: 時江東草創，盜賊多有，帝思所以防之，以問於循。

translations.literal: Early eastern rule faced bandits; the emperor asked prevention strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry plagued the new Jiangdong regime.

sentences.zh: 循答曰：「江道萬里，通涉五州，朝貢商旅之所來往也。

translations.literal: Xun answered: "The river course spans myriad li linking five provinces—the conduit of tribute and trade.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun began with riverine geography.

sentences.zh: 今議者欲出宣城以鎮江渚，或使諸縣領兵。

translations.literal: Some propose marching Xuancheng to guard shallows or arming every county.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xuancheng garrisons or county militias.

sentences.zh: 愚謂令長威弱，而兼才難備，發憚役之人，而禦之不肅，恐未必為用。

translations.literal: I deem magistrates weak and doubly talented rare—dragging fearful laborers yields slack defense—unlikely effective.
translations.idiomatic: Weak magistrates plus reluctant peasants make poor soldiers.

sentences.zh: 以循所聞，江中劇地惟有闔廬一處，地勢險奧，亡逃所聚。

translations.literal: What I know: the river's hotspot is Helü's narrows—terrain rugged, fugitives nest.
translations.idiomatic: Only Helü narrows concentrate river bandits.

sentences.zh: 特宜以重兵備戍，隨勢討除，絕其根帶。

translations.literal: Station crack troops there, adapt strikes, sever their roots.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy permanent garrisons could extirpate nests.

sentences.zh: 沿江諸縣各有分界，分界之內，官長所任，自可度土分力，多置亭行，恆使徼行，峻其綱目，嚴其刑賞，使越常科，勤則有殊榮之報，墮則有一身之罪，謂於大理不得不肅。

translations.literal: Each riverside county already has bounds—within them officials may gauge strength, multiply patrol posts, constant rounds, tighten statutes and punishments beyond usual statutes—diligence earns glory, slack invites personal guilt—thus discipline bites.
translations.idiomatic: County patrol grids with harsh carrot-and-stick beats vague mixed militias.

sentences.zh: 所給人以時番休，役不至困，代易有期。

translations.literal: Rotate reliefs so labor cycles and replacements stay predictable.
translations.idiomatic: Scheduled rotations prevent burnout.

sentences.zh: 案漢制十里一亭，亦以防禁切密故也。

translations.literal: Han placed a post every ten li precisely for tight prevention.
translations.idiomatic: Han's ten-li sentry posts modeled layered defense.

sentences.zh: 當今縱不能爾，要宜籌量，使力足相周。

translations.literal: Though we cannot replicate wholly, plan so forces mutually cover.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the principle even if not every ten li.

sentences.zh: 若寇劫強多，不能獨制者，可指其縱跡，言所在都督尋當致討。

translations.literal: When robbers mass beyond local control, trace trails so regional commanders may strike.
translations.idiomatic: Escalate to area command when bands swell.

sentences.zh: 今不明部分，使所在百姓與軍家雜其徼備，兩情俱墮，莫適任負，故所以徒有備名而不能為益者也。

translations.literal: Now unclear chains mix civilians and soldiers on patrol—both sides slack—no one accountable—hence empty precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Blurring civil-military patrol duty leaves everyone blameless and useless.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne adopted his river-security plan.

sentences.zh: 及湣帝即位，徵為宗正，元帝在鎮，又表為侍中，道險不行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended he summoned Xun as minister of imperial clan; Prince of Langye tabled concurrent palace attendant—dangerous roads blocked travel.
translations.idiomatic: Min-di summoned him as imperial clan minister; Yuan added attendant titles—travel stayed unsafe.

sentences.zh: 以討華軼功，將封鄉侯，循自以臥疾私門，固讓不受。

translations.literal: For merit against Hua Yi he was to receive township marquisate but pled sick seclusion and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused a Hua Yi victory fief citing domestic illness.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為中書令，加散騎常侍，又以老疾固辭。

translations.literal: Early Jianwu he became palace secretary director plus serving attendant-in-ordinary yet again cited age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu brought palace secretariat plus attendant honors—again declined.

sentences.zh: 帝下令曰：「孤以寡德，忝當大位，若涉巨川，罔知所憑。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We lack virtue yet occupy great rank as if fording a river without oar.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign admitted incompetence at the helm.

sentences.zh: 循言行以禮，乃時之望，俗之表也。

translations.literal: Xun's deportment embodies ritual—model of the age and folk.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun embodied ritual propriety society admired.

sentences.zh: 實賴其謀猷，以康萬機。

translations.literal: We truly depend on his counsel to harmonize myriad wheels.
translations.idiomatic: The court needed his steady counsel.

sentences.zh: 疾患有素，猶望臥相規輔，而固守捴謙，自陳懇至，此賢履信思順，苟以讓為高者也。

translations.literal: Though chronically ill we hoped he might advise from bed—yet stubborn modesty rings utterly sincere—such worthies prize yielding above fame.
translations.idiomatic: Even ill he should advise—but utter humility defines him.

sentences.zh: 今從其所執。

translations.literal: Now we yield to his insistence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor conceded.

sentences.zh: 」於是改拜太常，常侍如故。

translations.literal: " Therefore he was shifted to grand master of ceremonies while attendant title stayed.
translations.idiomatic: They reassigned him grand liturgist keeping attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 循以九卿舊不加官，今又疾患，不宜兼處此職，惟拜太常而已。

translations.literal: Because nine ministers traditionally lacked extra titles and illness lingered, dual posts seemed improper—he took grand liturgist alone.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted only grand liturgist to avoid plural offices.

sentences.zh: 時宗廟始建，舊儀多闕，或以惠懷二帝應各為世，則潁川世數過七，宜在迭毀。

translations.literal: As ancestral temples were founded old rites lacked detail—some argued Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai each formed generations so Yingchuan's column exceeded seven and deserved cyclical destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Temple succession debates invoked Hui vs Huai generations.

sentences.zh: 事下太常。

translations.literal: The matter went to the grand liturgist.
translations.idiomatic: Court referred ritual dispute to He Xun.

sentences.zh: 循議以為：

translations.literal: He Xun offered his formal opinion, stating:
translations.idiomatic: He Xun introduced his ritual ruling as follows:

sentences.zh: 禮，兄弟不相為後，不得以承代為世。

translations.literal: by ritual brothers do not succeed each other as generations—alternate succession cannot count as a reign line.
translations.idiomatic: brothers cannot stack as sequential ancestral generations.

sentences.zh: 殷之盤庚不序陽甲，漢之光武不繼成帝，別立廟寢，使臣下祭之，此前代之明典，而承繼之著義也。

translations.literal: Yin's Pan Geng did not rank Yang Jia; Han's Guangwu did not continue Cheng-di—they founded separate shrines for ministers to worship—classic precedent with clear succession meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Geng and Guangwu models demanded side chapels when succession skipped.

sentences.zh: 惠帝無後，懷帝承統，弟不後兄，則懷帝自上繼世祖，不繼惠帝，當同殷之陽甲，漢之成帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui lacked heirs; Emperor Huai inherited—not younger succeeding elder—thus Huai mounted directly from Shizu, not Hui; compare Yang Jia or Han Cheng-di cases.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-di's line should attach to Shizu rather than stack behind Hui-di—mirroring classical skips.

sentences.zh: 議者以聖德沖遠，未便改舊。

translations.literal: Those who argued held that, because the sage-virtue is profound and remote, it was not yet fitting to change the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Critics of change said His Majesty’s depth of virtue made it premature to overturn established temple precedent.

sentences.zh: 諸如此禮，通所未論。

translations.literal: As for rites such as these, the received consensus has never fully addressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Orthodox ritual handbooks had never squarely settled questions of this kind.

sentences.zh: 是以惠帝尚在太廟，而懷帝復人，數則盈八。

translations.literal: For this reason, while Emperor Hui was still enshrined in the Grand Temple, Emperor Huai entered as well, so the number of spirits exceeded eight.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Hui’s tablet remained in the Grand Temple when Emperor Huai was added, pushing the count past eight.

sentences.zh: 盈八之理，由惠帝不出，非上祖宜遷也。

translations.literal: The fact that the count exceeded eight arose because Emperor Hui had not been removed; it does not mean a senior ancestor ought to have been relocated.
translations.idiomatic: The roster went over eight only because Emperor Hui’s seat had not been vacated—not because a high forebear should have been displaced.

sentences.zh: 下世既升，上世乃遷，遷毀對代，不得相通，未有下升一世而上毀二世者也。

translations.literal: Once a junior generation is elevated, the senior generation is then removed; each removal keeps pace with its generation and must not be crossed—there has never been a case where the lower generation advanced one step while two senior generations were struck at once.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions and removals advance in lockstep across generations; never does one junior intake force the simultaneous demotion of two senior lines.

sentences.zh: 惠懷二帝俱繼世祖，兄弟旁親，同為一世，而上毀二為一世。

translations.literal: Emperors Hui and Huai both succeeded Emperor Shizu as brothers on a collateral branch; for temple reckoning they occupy a single generation, yet above them two ancestors were removed as if only one generation had turned over.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Huai succeeded Shizu as fraternal heirs, so they count as one generation in the shrine, yet two higher tablets were cleared as if that were a single generational shift.

sentences.zh: 今以惠帝之崩已毀豫章，懷帝之入復毀潁川，如此則一世再遷，祖位橫析。

translations.literal: Now Emperor Hui’s death has already removed the Yuzhang seat, and Emperor Huai’s enshrinement again removes the Yingchuan seat—thus one generation is relocated twice and ancestral positions are split askew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang fell when Emperor Hui died, and Yingchuan is to fall again for Emperor Huai—one generation thus suffers two removals and breaks the ancestral rows.

sentences.zh: 求之古義，未見此例。

translations.literal: Searched against ancient principle, this pattern has no precedent.
translations.idiomatic: No classical warrant supports such an arrangement.

sentences.zh: 惠帝宜出，尚未輕論，況可輕毀一祖而無義例乎？

translations.literal: That Emperor Hui ought to leave has not even been treated as a light matter; how much less may one rashly remove an ancestor without a binding exemplar?
translations.idiomatic: Whether Emperor Hui should be removed is already a grave issue—far less may we cast out an ancestor with no clear rule to cite.

sentences.zh: 潁川既無可毀之理，則見神之數居然自八，此盡有由而然，非謂數之常也。

translations.literal: Since Yingchuan cannot rightly be removed on principle, the manifest spirits naturally number eight; this is entirely due to contingent causes, not the constant, proper number.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan should not be vacated, so eight spirits sit in the temple by circumstance—not because eight is the canonical quota.

sentences.zh: 既有八神，則不得不於七室之外權安一位也。

translations.literal: Once eight spirits are served, one cannot but provisionally add a ninth place outside the seven bays.
translations.idiomatic: With eight spirits to house, the court must squeeze an extra niche beyond the seven canonical chambers.

sentences.zh: 至尊于惠懷俱是兄弟，自上後世祖，不繼二帝，則二帝之神行應別出，不為廟中恆有八室也。

translations.literal: The sovereign stands as brother to both Emperors Hui and Huai and, ascending after Shizu, does not succeed those two directly; their tablets should therefore be moved out separately, not leave the temple permanently fixed at eight bays.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty is brother to Hui and Huai and inherits from Shizu, not from them; their spirits ought to exit the main sequence rather than lock the temple at eight shrines forever.

sentences.zh: 又武帝初成太廟時，正神止七，而楊元後之神亦權立一室。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Emperor Wu first completed the Grand Temple, orthodox seats numbered only seven, yet the spirit of Empress Yuan of Yang was also given a provisional chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu founded the Grand Temple, only seven legitimate seats existed, yet Empress Dowager Yang Yuan’s spirit was granted a temporary bay.

sentences.zh: 永熙元年，告世祖諡於太廟八室，此是苟有八神，不拘於七之舊例也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, Shizu’s posthumous title was proclaimed across eight temple chambers—showing that whenever eight spirits must be honored, one is not shackled to the old rule of seven.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 1 saw Shizu’s posthumous title read in eight bays, proof that the rule of seven yields whenever eight ancestors must be served.

sentences.zh: 又議者以景帝俱已在廟，則惠懷一例。

translations.literal: Some debaters further argued that because Emperor Jing is already in the temple, Emperors Hui and Huai should be handled the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Others claimed that because Emperor Jing already has a place, Hui and Huai deserve identical treatment.

sentences.zh: 景帝盛德元功，王基之本，義著祖宗，百世不毀，故所以特在本廟，且亦世代尚近，數得相容，安神而已，無逼上祖，如王氏昭穆既滿，終應別廟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing’s towering virtue and founding merit anchor the royal house; his merit is registered among the ancestors and exempts him from removal for generations; he therefore holds a special seat in this temple, and because his age is still comparatively near, his presence can be reconciled with the overall count—it merely settles his spirit without crowding a senior forebear; when the Wang house’s zhao and mu lanes filled, they finally opened a separate shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing’s foundational merit earns him a permanent bay that does not squeeze out elders—rather like the Wang clan, which spun off an auxiliary temple once its zhao-mu columns were full.

sentences.zh: 以今方之，既輕重義異，又七廟七世之親；

translations.literal: Measured against the present case, the moral weight differs, and the seven temples mark seven generations of kinship;
translations.idiomatic: Set beside today’s problem, the equities are not the same, and the seven-shrine rule tracks seven generations of descent.

sentences.zh: 昭穆，父子位也。

translations.literal: Zhao and mu are the positions of father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The zhao and mu rows designate father-and-son alternation in the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 若當兄弟旁滿，輒毀上祖，則祖位空懸，世數不足，何取於三昭三穆與太祖之廟然後成七哉！

translations.literal: If, whenever a collateral generation of brothers fills the line, one strikes the senior ancestor, then higher seats stand empty and the generational tally collapses—what becomes of three zhao, three mu, plus the Grand Progenitor’s shrine in forming seven?
translations.idiomatic: If each fraternal cohort triggers removal of the eldest line, the upper ranks go hollow and the count fails—how then do three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Progenitor ever make seven?

sentences.zh: 今七廟之義，出於王氏。

translations.literal: Today the theory of the seven temples derives from the Wang imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine of seven ancestral shrines itself comes from the Jin royal Wang pattern.

sentences.zh: 從禰以上至於高祖，親廟四世，高祖以上復有五世六世無服之祖，故為三昭三穆並太祖而七也。

translations.literal: From the mitzu shrine up through the high ancestor are four generations of close temples; above the high ancestor stand fifth- and sixth-generation forebears beyond mourning grades; hence three zhao, three mu, together with the Grand Progenitor, make seven.
translations.idiomatic: Four intimate shrines run from one’s late father to the high ancestor; beyond them lie fifth- and sixth-generation ancestors out of mourning— yielding three zhao bays, three mu bays, and the Grand Progenitor for seven in all.

sentences.zh: 故世祖郊定廟禮，京兆、潁川會、高之親，豫章五世，征西六世，以應此義。

translations.literal: Therefore Shizu, when fixing suburban and temple rites, aligned the Jingzhao and Yingchuan seats with the generational closeness due to Princes Hui and Gao, reckoned Yuzhang at five generations, and the Western Expedition marquis at six, to match that scheme.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Shizu calibrated the Jingzhao and Yingchuan niches to the kinship tiers of Princes Hui and Gao, placed Yuzhang five generations out, and the Western Expedition ancestor at six.

sentences.zh: 今至尊繼統，亦宜有五六世之祖，豫章六世，潁川五世，俱不應毀。

translations.literal: Now the reigning sovereign continues the line and likewise ought to retain forebears across five or six generations; Yuzhang sits at six generations, Yingchuan at five—neither should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning emperor inherits the same five- or six-generation span: Yuzhang belongs six generations back, Yingchuan five, so neither tablet should be struck.

sentences.zh: 今既云豫章先毀，又當重毀潁川，此為廟中之親惟從高祖已下，無復高祖以上二世之祖，于王氏之義，三昭三穆廢闕其二，其非宗廟之本所據承，又違世祖祭征西、豫章之意，于一王定禮所闕不少。

translations.literal: Now that Yuzhang is said to be removed first and Yingchuan must be removed again, the temple’s close kin run only from the high ancestor downward, with no two generations above the high ancestor; by the Wang-house reading, two of the three zhao and three mu are voided; this cannot be what the ancestral temple’s foundation inherits, and it contravenes Shizu’s intent in sacrificing to the Western Expedition and Yuzhang ancestors—for a single dynasty’s ritual code the omissions would be grave.
translations.idiomatic: Striking Yuzhang and then Yingchuan leaves only kin from the high ancestor down, erasing two generations above him and breaking two-thirds of the zhao-mu grid—betraying the temple’s basis and Shizu’s will to honor the Western Expedition and Yuzhang lines, with massive gaps for any stable rite.

sentences.zh: 時尚書僕射刁協與循異議，循答義深備，辭多不載，竟從循議焉。

translations.literal: At the time Deputy Director of the Secretariat Diao Xie differed from He Xun; He Xun’s replies were thorough and tightly principled, and most of his wording is not recorded; in the end the court adopted He Xun’s view.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie, the Secretariat’s deputy director, disagreed with He Xun, whose counterarguments were exhaustive though largely omitted from the record; the court followed He Xun.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑滯皆諮之於循，循輒依經禮而對，為當世儒宗。

translations.literal: Whenever court business stuck on ritual, it was put to He Xun, who answered always from canonical ceremony and became the age’s leading Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: The government consulted He Xun on every deadlock, and he answered from the classics, standing as foremost scholar of the day.

sentences.zh: 其後帝以循清貧，下令曰：「循冰清玉潔，行為俗表，位處上卿，而居身服物蓋周形而已，屋室財庇風雨。孤近造其廬，以為慨然。其賜六尺床薦席褥並錢二十萬，以表至德，暢孤意焉。」循又讓，不許，不得已留之，初不服用。

translations.literal: Later, deeming He Xun poor in possessions, the emperor issued an edict: "He Xun is ice-clear and jade-pure, conduct models custom though office ranks among chief ministers—yet his clothing covers barely his limbs and his roof only shields wind and rain. Visiting his hut lately moved me sorely. Grant him a six-foot couch with mats, bedding, and two hundred thousand cash to honor supreme virtue and voice my intent." He Xun declined again; refusal went unheard; forced to keep them he never wore or spent the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Learning He Xun lived in deliberate poverty, the sovereign sent bedding and cash with effusive praise; He Xun tried to send everything back, failed, and left the bounty untouched.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐位，有司奏琅邪恭王宜稱皇考，循又議曰：「案禮子不敢以己爵加父。」帝納之。

translations.literal: When the emperor assumed the throne the bureaucracy urged that the Cultured Prince of Langye merit the title imperial father; He Xun argued: "By ritual a son may not add his own noble rank atop his father." The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: On accession debate erupted over posthumous honors for Prince Gong of Langye; He Xun cited ritual—a son cannot inflate his father's station—and the ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄以循行太子太傅，太常如故。

translations.literal: Soon He Xun was named acting Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent while remaining Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun was shortly appointed acting Grand Tutor to the crown prince and kept his Grand Master of Ceremonies post.

sentences.zh: 循自以枕疾廢頓，臣節不修，上隆降尊之義，不替交敘之敬，懼非垂典之教也，累表固讓。

translations.literal: He Xun deemed himself broken by chronic sickbed illness and unable to uphold ministerial bearing; to accept lofty rank without adjusting the courtesies between higher and lower, he feared, would violate exemplary teaching, so he repeatedly begged leave to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Believing long illness disqualified him from proper ministerial conduct, He Xun feared that taking honor without reordering mutual deference would break canonical example and repeatedly refused the promotion.

sentences.zh: 帝以循體德率物，有不言之益，敦厲備至，期於不許，命皇太子親往拜焉。

translations.literal: The emperor prized He Xun’s silent moral influence, pressed him with every kindness, intended never to grant a refusal, and ordered the crown prince to visit and bow to him in person.
translations.idiomatic: The throne valued his wordless moral example, urged him relentlessly, would hear no refusal, and sent the heir apparent to pay formal respects at his home.

sentences.zh: 循有羸疾，而恭於接對；

translations.literal: He Xun bore wasting illness, yet was reverent in receiving visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Though chronically frail, He Xun still received guests with painstaking courtesy.

sentences.zh: 詔斷賓客，其崇遇如此。

translations.literal: An edict cut off visitors; such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders barred callers to spare him—such was the esteem he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 疾漸篤，表乞骸骨，上還印綬，改授左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His illness worsened; he memorialized to surrender office, return his seals and ribbons, and was reassigned Left Brilliant Counselor with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: As he sickened he asked to retire, handed back his credentials, and was shifted to Left Brilliant Counselor and opening-office privilege equal to the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 帝臨軒，遣使持節，加印綬。

translations.literal: The emperor appeared at the gallery and sent an envoy with staff of office to invest him with new seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: From the front gallery the ruler dispatched a credentialed messenger to confer fresh seals and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 循雖口不能言，指麾左右，推去章服。

translations.literal: Though He Xun could no longer speak, he gestured to attendants and pushed away the court regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to speak, he still signed to servants and thrust away the insignia robes.

sentences.zh: 車駕親幸，執手流涕。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited in person; the emperor clasped his hand and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign came himself, held his hand, and shed tears.

sentences.zh: 太子親臨者三焉，往還皆拜，儒者以為榮。

translations.literal: The heir apparent came in person three times; each arrival and departure involved bows; scholars counted it supreme honor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince called on him thrice, bowing comings and goings—scholars deemed it unparalleled glory.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 帝素服舉哀，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain mourning and wept bitterly for him.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler went into undyed mourning and mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works with the posthumous epithet Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Mu (‘Solemn’).

sentences.zh: 將葬，帝又出臨其柩，哭之盡哀，遣兼侍御史持節監護。

translations.literal: When the burial neared, the emperor again approached the coffin, mourned to the full limit of grief, and assigned an acting palace aide with credentials to supervise the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Before interment the sovereign returned to the bier, grieved his fill, and detailed an acting attendant censor with staff to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 皇太子追送近途，望船流涕。

translations.literal: The crown prince escorted him to the shore, watched the barge depart, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent saw him to the riverbank and wept as the boat bearing his remains sailed away.

sentences.zh: 循少玩篇籍，善屬文，博覽眾書，尤精禮傳。

translations.literal: In youth He Xun delighted in texts, excelled at composition, read broadly, and was especially adept at ritual commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved books, wrote well, ranged wide in reading, and mastered the ritual classics above all.

sentences.zh: 雅有知人之鑒，拔同郡楊方於卑陋，卒成名於世。

translations.literal: He had a fine eye for talent, raising fellow townsman Yang Fang from obscurity to eventual fame in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He recognized ability, plucking Yang Fang of his commandery from low status until Yang’s name spread empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 子隰，康帝時官至臨海太守。

translations.literal: His son Xi rose under Emperor Kang to Grand Warden of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi, under Emperor Kang, became Grand Warden of Linhai.

translations.literal: Attached subsection.
translations.idiomatic: An appended biography follows.

sentences.zh: 楊方

translations.literal: Yang Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang (supplementary notice).

sentences.zh: 楊方，字公回。

translations.literal: (Heading) Yang Fang, style Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang, whose courtesy name was Gonghui,

sentences.zh: 少好學，有異才。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and possessed unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was devoted to study and showed rare ability.

sentences.zh: 初為郡鈴下威儀，公事之暇，輒讀《五經》，鄉邑未之知。

translations.literal: At first he served as the commandery’s bell usher for ceremony; in spare time from official duties he constantly read the Five Classics; his township did not yet know of him.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a low ceremonial runner for the county; off duty he pored over the Five Classics, still unknown at home.

sentences.zh: 內史諸葛恢見而奇之，待以門人之禮，由是始得周旋貴人間。

translations.literal: Interior Clerk Zhuge Hui saw him and deemed him extraordinary, treated him with disciple’s rites, and thereby he began to move among the great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui, interior clerk, spotted his gift, took him as a pupil, and introduced him among the powerful.

sentences.zh: 時虞喜兄弟以儒學立名，雅愛方，為之延譽。

translations.literal: At the time the Yu Xi brothers were famed for Confucian learning; they sincerely favored Fang and spread his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu brothers, celebrated scholars, genuinely championed him and praised him abroad.

sentences.zh: 恢嘗遣方為文，薦郡功曹主簿。

translations.literal: Zhuge Hui once had Fang draft a piece and recommended him for merit clerk and chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui once commissioned a composition from him and sponsored him for merit clerk and chief clerk posts.

sentences.zh: 虞預稱美之，送以示循。

translations.literal: Yu Yu praised the work and sent it to He Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu acclaimed the essay and forwarded it to He Xun.

sentences.zh: 循報書曰：「此子開拔有志，意只言異於凡猥耳，不圖偉才如此。

translations.literal: He Xun replied in a letter: ‘This youth has been advanced with high purpose; I had intended only to say he rises above the vulgar herd; I did not expect such towering talent.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun answered: ‘I meant merely to note promise beyond the common run—I never imagined genius of this order.’

sentences.zh: 其文甚有奇分，若出其胸臆，乃是一國所推，豈但牧豎中逸群邪！

translations.literal: His writing shows striking originality, as if straight from the heart; he is talent a whole domain would praise—how could he be only the best among herdsboys!’
translations.idiomatic: His prose is strikingly fresh, seemingly unmediated; the realm would acclaim him—far more than first among rustics!’

sentences.zh: 聞處舊黨之中，好有謙沖之行，此亦立身之一隅。

translations.literal: I hear that among old associates he keeps modest, yielding conduct—that too is one facet of self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: They say he remains humble among longtime friends—one mark of character.

sentences.zh: 然世衰道喪，人物凋弊，每聞一介之徒有向道之志，冀之願之。

translations.literal: Yet the age declines and the Way is lost; men of quality wither; whenever I hear of someone of slender means turning toward the Way, I hope for him and root for him.
translations.idiomatic: In a decayed age of thinning talent, every report of a humble man seeking the Way heartens me.

sentences.zh: 如方者乃荒萊之特苗，鹵田之善秀，姿質已良，但沾染未足耳；

translations.literal: A man like Fang is a rare shoot in waste scrub, a fine ear in briny soil—native stuff already sound, only needing fuller polish;
translations.idiomatic: Fang is choice grain sprung from untilled ground—raw talent sound, still wanting polish,

sentences.zh: 移植豐壤，必成嘉豎。

translations.literal: transplant him to rich earth and he will surely become an excellent stalk.
translations.idiomatic: set him in fertile soil and he will ripen into prize grain.

sentences.zh: 足下才為世英，位為朝右，道隆化立，然後為貴。

translations.literal: You, sir, rank as the age’s exemplar and stand at the court’s summit; only when the Way towers and transformation is achieved is true nobility realized.
translations.idiomatic: You unite the day’s foremost talent with chief place at court—true greatness means exalting the Way and shaping custom.

sentences.zh: 昔許子將拔樊仲昭于賈堅，郭林宗成魏德公於畎畝。

translations.literal: Anciently Xu Shao lifted Fan Yan from market toil, and Guo Tai made Wei Ji from the furrows.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Shao raised Fan Zhongzhao from the stalls, and Guo Tai crowned Wei Degong from the plowland.

sentences.zh: 足下志隆此業，二賢之功不為難及也。

translations.literal: If you, sir, set your will on this calling, matching those two worthies is not beyond reach.’
translations.idiomatic: If you aim that high, equaling those two mentors lies within reach.’

sentences.zh: 」循遂稱方于京師。

translations.literal: He Xun therefore praised Fang in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With that He Xun championed Fang at court.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導辟為掾，轉東安太守，遷司徒參軍事。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Dao summoned him as an aide, transferred him to Grand Warden of Dong’an, then promoted him to staff officer on the minister’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao took him on as a ministerial aide, moved him to Grand Warden of Dong’an, then to staff officer on the minister’s staff.

sentences.zh: 方在都邑，搢紳之士咸厚遇之，自以地寒，不願久留京華，求補遠郡，欲閒居著述。

translations.literal: In the capital the gentry with sashes all treated him generously; he considered his origins humble, was unwilling to remain long in the capital splendor, sought appointment to a distant commandery, and wished to live at leisure composing scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Elites welcomed him warmly in Luoyang, but mindful of modest birth he sought a distant post rather than linger at court, intending quiet writing.

sentences.zh: 導從之，上補高梁太守。

translations.literal: Wang Dao consented and had him named Grand Warden of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao agreed and secured him the Gaoliang magistracy.

sentences.zh: 在郡積年，著《五經鉤沈》，更撰《吳越春秋》，並雜文筆，皆行於世。

translations.literal: In the commandery for many years he authored *Gleanings from the Five Classics*, rewrote *Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue*, and assorted essays, all of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: There he spent years producing *Gleanings from the Five Classics*, a new *Annals of Wu and Yue*, and various pieces that won wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 以年老，棄郡歸。

translations.literal: Because of old age he resigned the commandery and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In age he gave up the post and went home.

sentences.zh: 導將進之台閣，固辭還鄉里，終於家。

translations.literal: Wang Dao intended to advance him to the central terrace; he firmly declined, returned to his home village, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao tried to pull him to the capital bench, he refused, withdrew to his district, and ended his days at home.

sentences.zh: 薛兼

translations.literal: Xue Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jian (biography).

sentences.zh: 薛兼，字令長，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Xue Jian, style Lingzhang, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jian, courtesy name Lingzhang, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖綜，仕吳為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zong had served Eastern Wu as Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zong had been Wu’s Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父瑩，有名吳朝。

translations.literal: His father Ying was renowned at the Wu court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying was celebrated in the Wu bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 吳平，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After Wu fell he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu submitted he was named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 兼清素有器宇，少與同郡紀瞻、廣陵閔鴻、吳郡顧榮、會稽賀循齊名，號為「五俊」。

translations.literal: Jian was pure and restrained with lofty bearing; in youth he shared renown with Ji Zhan of his commandery, Min Hong of Guangling, Gu Rong of Wu, and He Xun of Kuaiji— styled the ‘five outstanding.’
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jian, chaste in habit and imposing in manner, was grouped in youth with Ji Zhan, Min Hong, Gu Rong, and He Xun as the ‘Five Paragons.’

sentences.zh: 初入洛，司空張華見而奇之，曰：「皆南金也。

translations.literal: On first entering Luoyang, Minister of Works Zhang Hua saw them and marveled, saying: ‘All are southern gold.’
translations.idiomatic: When they first reached Luoyang, Zhang Hua, Minister of Works, exclaimed: ‘Each is treasure from the south.’

sentences.zh: 」察河南孝謙，辟公府，除比陽相，蒞任有能名。

translations.literal: ’ Assessed on the Henan filial-and-incorrupt roster, he was summoned to princely offices, appointed chancellor of Biyang, and gained a name for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Recommended from Henan’s filial-incorrupt list, he entered princely service, became Biyang’s chancellor, and earned repute for competence.

sentences.zh: 曆太子洗馬、散騎常侍、懷令。

translations.literal: He successively served as groom-liberian to the heir apparent, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and magistrate of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through groom attendant to the heir apparent, cavalier attendant, and Huai county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 司空、東海王越引為參軍，轉祭酒，賜爵安陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Prince of Donghai Sima Yue took him as military adviser, transferred him to libationer, and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Minister of Works and prince of Donghai, enrolled him as staff adviser, promoted him to libationer, and made him village marquis of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，以為軍諮祭酒，稍遷丞相長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was General Who Guards the East, Jian became military libationer and gradually rose to chief clerk of the princely counselor.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan of Jin held the eastern command, Xue Jian served as army libationer and advanced to chief clerk of the prime minister’s bureau.

sentences.zh: 甚勤王事，以上佐祿優，每自約損，取周而已。

translations.literal: He was extremely diligent in royal affairs; because a senior aide’s salary was ample, he habitually tightened his own expenses and took only enough for sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into service yet, though handsomely paid as chief aide, lived sparely and kept only what he needed.

sentences.zh: 進爵安陽鄉侯，拜丹陽太守。

translations.literal: He was advanced to district marquis of Anyang and appointed Grand Warden of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to district marquis of Anyang and named Grand Warden of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 中興建，轉尹，加秩中二千石，遷尚書，領太子少傅。

translations.literal: After the restoration he became capital intendant at two-thousand-shi mid grade, was promoted Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty revived he turned capital intendant at two thousand shi, then Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Junior Tutorship of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 自綜至兼，三世傅東宮，談者美之。

translations.literal: From Zong through Jian, three generations tutored the Eastern Palace; contemporaries praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Three successive generations—Zong to Jian—served the heir apparent’s household, to general admiration.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，王敦表兼為太常。

translations.literal: Early in Yongchang, Wang Dun memorialized Jian as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Yongchang, Wang Dun recommended him for Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Jian was additionally named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ming’s accession brought Jian an added title as cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝以東宮時師傅，猶宜盡敬，乃下詔曰：「朕以不德，夙遭閔凶。

translations.literal: Because Jian had been tutor while the sovereign was crown prince, full reverence still seemed proper; the emperor therefore issued an edict: ‘I lack virtue and long ago met grievous loss.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xue Jian had instructed him as heir, the emperor deemed utmost deference fitting and proclaimed: ‘Mine is no virtue; early I suffered bitter bereavement.'

sentences.zh: 猥以眇身，托于王公之上。

translations.literal: Mean though my slight person may be, it is set above the great princes.’
translations.idiomatic: This frail self has been mounted above the kingly dukes.’

sentences.zh: 哀煢在疚，靡所諮仰，憂懷惴惴，如臨于谷。

translations.literal: Orphaned and sick at heart, I have none to consult or lean upon; anxiety grips me as though I stood above a deep ravine.’
translations.idiomatic: I mourn alone, ill with grief, with no counsellor to lean on, and dread weighs on me like treading the lip of a deep gorge.’

sentences.zh: 孔子有云：『故雖天子，必有尊也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: ‘Even the Son of Heaven has someone whom he honors.’
translations.idiomatic: As Confucius put it, even the Son of Heaven must honor someone above himself.’

sentences.zh: 』朕將祗奉先師之禮，以諮有德。

translations.literal: I shall reverently uphold the rites owed former teachers and consult men of virtue.’
translations.idiomatic: I will keep the courtesies due my old tutors and seek guidance from the worthy.’

sentences.zh: 太宰西陽王秩尊望重，在貴思降。

translations.literal: The Grand Mentor, Prince of Xiyang, holds exalted rank and high esteem, yet in nobility remembers to humble himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Mentor and Prince of Xiyang bears supreme dignity yet knows modesty befitting his station.

sentences.zh: 丞相武昌公、司空即丘子體道高邈，勳德兼備，先帝執友，朕之師傅。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wuchang, chief minister, and the Minister of Works, Marquis of Qiqiu, embody the loftiest Way, combine merit with virtue, were clasped friends of the late emperor, and served as my own tutors.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister, Duke of Wuchang, and the Minister of Works, Marquis of Qiqiu, unite transcendent principle with shining achievement, befriended my late father, and taught me on the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太常安陽鄉侯訓保朕躬，忠肅篤誠。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies and Marquis of Anyang instructed and guarded my person with loyal, solemn earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies and the Marquis of Anyang reared and shielded me with steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 夫崇親尊賢，先帝所重，朕見四君及書疏儀體，一如東宮故事。

translations.literal: To exalt kin and honor worthies was what the late emperor stressed; toward these four gentlemen, in every memorial and ritual form, I shall behave exactly as in Eastern Palace precedent.’
translations.idiomatic: Veneration of kin and esteem for teachers, as my father urged, means I owe these four the same courtesies I showed them as crown prince.’

sentences.zh: 」是歲，卒。

translations.literal: That same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away later that same year.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太常、安陽鄉侯兼履德沖素，盡忠恪己。

translations.literal: An edict declared: ‘Grand Master of Ceremonies and Marquis of Anyang, Jian, practices plain, understated virtue and devotes himself with loyal self-discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The throne announced: ‘Grand Master of Ceremonies and Marquis of Anyang Xue Jian lives in unadorned integrity and serves with scrupulous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 方賴德訓，弘濟政道，不幸殂殞，痛於厥心。

translations.literal: I had just relied on his moral instruction to widen and sustain the government; unluckily he has died; pain fills my heart.’
translations.idiomatic: I looked to his counsel to steady the realm; his sudden death grieves me deeply.’

sentences.zh: 今遣持節侍御史贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Now we dispatch an attendant censor bearing insignia to confer posthumously grand master of the left with privilege opening a separate headquarters matching the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a ranking censor with credentials to posthumously award grand counselor of the left plus Three Offices matching privileges.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉茲榮寵。

translations.literal: If soul and consciousness endure, may they delight in this splendid favor.
translations.idiomatic: Should awareness linger beyond death, let it take comfort in such imperial munificence.

sentences.zh: 」及葬，屬王敦作逆，朝廷多故，不得議諡，直遣使者祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: Closing the edict: when burial came Wang Dun rebelled and court crises multiplied—posthumous deliberation proved impossible, so envoys were simply sent to offer the grand sacrifice of ox, sheep, and hog.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's coup stalled the usual epithet debates at burial—only a capital envoy arrived with the grand Three Victims offering.

sentences.zh: 子顒，先兼卒，無後。

translations.literal: His son Yong died before him without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yong predeceased him and left no successor.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：元帝樹基淮海，百度權輿，夢想群材，共康庶績。

translations.literal: The historians observed: Yuan emperor planted foundations beside Huai and Hai while myriad measures were germinating; he dreamed of assembling talents to jointly secure orderly accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers wrote that Sima Rui's southeastern base—everything still nascent—craved capable ministers to steady rule.

sentences.zh: 顧、紀、賀、薛等並南金東箭，世胄高門，委質霸朝，豫聞邦政；

translations.literal: Gu, Ji, He, and Xue together were southern gold and eastern arrowwood—sons of eminent gates—who pledged themselves to the hegemon court and took part in governing policy.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, Ji Zhan, He Xun, and Xue Jian embodied southern excellence from old elite houses and stepped straight into the protector administration.

sentences.zh: 典憲資其刊輯，帷幄佇其謀猷；

translations.literal: Statutes relied on their pruning and collation; inner chambers awaited their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: They trimmed legal drafts while military planners hung on their memoranda.

sentences.zh: 望重搢紳，任惟元凱，官成名立，光國榮家。

translations.literal: Revered amid sash-and-belt circles, charged like ancient pillar ministers—titles secured and fame established—they glorified state and clan alike.
translations.idiomatic: Their prestige anchored gentry opinion; posts matched archetypal ministers until careers crowned both dynasty and lineage.

sentences.zh: 非惟感會所鐘，抑亦材能斯至。

translations.literal: Not only did auspicious fortune smile—they possessed talent ample enough to earn it.
translations.idiomatic: Timing helped, yet their abilities genuinely measured up.

sentences.zh: 而循位登保傅，朝望特隆，遂使鑾蹕降臨，承明下拜。

translations.literal: He Xun moreover climbed tutor ranks with unrivaled court esteem until imperial carriages called at his door and attendants bowed within Chenming halls.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun's ascent to grand tutor drew sedan visits and palace bows rare even among famed tutors.

sentences.zh: 雖西漢之恩崇張禹，東都之禮重桓榮，弗是過也。

translations.literal: Though Western Han showered Zhang Yu or eastern capital honored Huan Rong, neither episode surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhang Yu's bounty or Later Han Huan Rong's ritual nod hardly exceeds such ceremony.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：彥先通識，思遠方直。

translations.literal: The encomium declares: Yanxian broadly discerning; Siyuan square as a carpenter's line.
translations.idiomatic: The verse pairs Gu Rong's panoramic judgment with Ji Zhan's blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 薛既清貞，賀惟學植。

translations.literal: Xue stayed lucid and pure; He alone rooted deep in classical cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jian shimmered with icy clarity; He Xun embodied ritual scholarship.

sentences.zh: 逢時遇主，摶風矯翼。

translations.literal: Encountering their moment and lord they mounted the gale with spreading wings.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the right age and ruler, soaring like hawks on the storm.
